1	# SC1 — Closed Spec Properties (SP-1..SP-7)
2	
3	- **Version**: 1.0
4	- **Date**: 2026-05-04
5	- **Status**: Proposal
6	- **Precipitating incident(s)**: [INC-1 — The Simple-Fix Contamination](../INCIDENTS/simple-fix-contamination.md)
7	- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation)
8	- **Applies to**: every project that has declared a shippable phase (Phase I or later)
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Problem statement
13	
14	Permissive specs admit drift additively. An agent (or operator) who wants to
15	add a feature, a sealed-class variant, a composable, or a checklist task can do
16	so by *appending* to the existing `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` + `CHECKLIST.md` —
17	even when the addition materially changes Phase scope or entity-table shape.
18	
19	The result is **retroactive legitimization**: the spec grows to match whatever
20	code shipped, rather than constraining what the code may ship. The single
21	source of truth becomes a scribe of the tree, not a governor of it.
22	
23	The incident at `INC-1` traces one concrete occurrence: a "simple add a
24	progress bar" ask produced ~700 lines of DL prose, in-place entity-table
25	edits, a new composable, a new screen, and seven checklist tasks — all
26	admitted additively, none stopped by the existing spec's own shape. The
27	current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` global rules (I-1 through I-6) describe the
28	correct workflow but rely on agent discipline to enforce it. Agent discipline
29	is insufficient; the drift fires at exactly the moments when the agent's
30	immediate "helpfulness" instinct is strongest and discipline is weakest.
31	
32	This convention **moves enforcement from agent behaviour to spec shape**. A
33	closed spec refuses the drift at write time. The agent does not need to
34	remember the sequence; the sequence is the only path the spec permits.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## The seven properties
39	
40	Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the closed
41	form required, (c) the structural effect on `INC-1`.
42	
43	### SP-1 — Closed-set declarations on every enumeration
44	
45	Every sealed class, enum, or finite variant set in the entity table must carry
46	an explicit closure marker naming the Phase at which it was closed.
47	
48	**Permissive form** (currently allowed in DeepScriber `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`
49	§6.3 line 1044):
50	
51	> `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | … | `Idle, Downloading(...), Loading, Ready, Error(message)` (per DL-12 — `Downloading` variant added …)
52	
53	**Closed form required**:
54	
55	> `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | … | **Closed set, Phase I:** `Idle, Loading, Ready, Error(message)`. Addition of a variant is a Phase boundary event and requires a new AD (not a DL).
56	
57	**Effect on INC-1**: Adding `Downloading` would not be a DL-level edit; it
58	would require either a new AD (alternatives/choice/rationale round, operator
59	approval) or Phase II deferral. The "just add a variant" path does not exist.
60	
61	### SP-2 — Phase scope enumerated and closed
62	
63	`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md §1` or a new `§1.5 Phase I Feature Manifest` must
64	enumerate the **exact** set of user-visible and developer-visible features in
65	Phase I, and declare it **CLOSED**.
66	
67	**Closed form required**:
68	
69	> **Phase I feature manifest (CLOSED):**
70	> 1. Audio capture + VAD chunking
71	> 2. On-device transcription (engine per AD-n)
72	> 3. Phase I tools (count per AD-10)
73	> 4. Two-pass inference (per AD-5)
74	> 5. Post-recording diarization (per AD-3)
75	> 6. Session history + annotation editing
76	> 7. KB ingestion (path per AD-15)
77	> 8. Entitlement gating
78	>
79	> Any feature not in this list is Phase II or later. Lifting a feature from
80	> Phase II to Phase I requires a new AD *and* a documented phase-boundary
81	> review, not a DL.
82	
83	**Effect on INC-1**: The line in DL-12 — *"lifted from 'Phase II refinement'
84	to Phase I scope"* — would fail the phase-boundary gate. The progress-bar UX
85	would remain Phase II until a proper AD promoted it.
86	
87	### SP-3 — DL authority is bounded; DLs cannot change scope
88	
89	DLs (Decision Log entries) are explicitly **post-AD clarifications**, not
90	alternatives to ADs. Their charter:
91	
92	> A DL resolves an ambiguity, contradiction, or wave-2 halt *within* the
93	> existing AD + entity-table envelope. A DL cannot:
94	> - Add a variant to a closed set (SP-1).
95	> - Add a feature to a closed phase manifest (SP-2).
96	> - Add an entity-table row that no AD authorizes (SP-7).
97	> - Promote scope from a later phase to the current phase (SP-2).
98	>
99	> Any DL that attempts the above must be promoted to an AD (with alternatives,
100	> choice, rationale, operator approval) before it can land.
101	
102	**Effect on INC-1**: DL-12 performs all four forbidden operations. It adds a
103	variant (`Downloading`), adds features (non-blocking load + progress UI +
104	gating matrix), adds entity-table rows (`LlmStatusIndicator`), and promotes
105	scope. Under SP-3 it is rejected at write time and must be rewritten as AD-17
106	with the full authorization round.
107	
108	### SP-4 — Entity-table completeness gate (CI-enforced)
109	
110	A CI check verifies that every source file in the tracked language(s) has
111	exactly one `File:line` citation in the entity table, and every entity-table
112	`File:line` citation points at a file that exists.
113	
114	**CI rule (example for a Kotlin project)**:
115	
116	```bash
117	# Orphan check: files in tree with no entity-table citation
118	comm -23 \
119	  <(git ls-files '*.kt' | sort -u) \
120	  <(grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z/._-]+\.kt:[0-9]+`' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md \
121	    | sed 's/:[0-9]*`$//; s/^`//' \
122	    | sort -u) \
123	  | grep . && { echo "ORPHAN FILES — every .kt file must have a §6 entity-table row"; exit 1; }
124	
125	# Stranded check: citations with no file
126	comm -13 \
127	  <(git ls-files '*.kt' | sort -u) \
128	  <(grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z/._-]+\.kt:[0-9]+`' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md \
129	    | sed 's/:[0-9]*`$//; s/^`//' \
130	    | sort -u) \
131	  | grep . && { echo "STRANDED CITATIONS — entity-table row points at non-existent file"; exit 1; }
132	```
133	
134	Adapt the glob pattern and citation regex per project language. The invariant
135	is **1:1 correspondence** between tracked-source files and entity-table
136	citations.
137	
138	**Effect on INC-1**: `SplashScreen.kt` could not be committed, because CI
139	would report it as an orphan (no §6.7 row). The Class B contamination (as
140	classified in INC-1) becomes structurally impossible.
141	
142	### SP-5 — Checklist STEP closure
143	
144	Each STEP in `CHECKLIST.md` declares its task inventory as closed:
145	
146	**Closed form required**:
147	
148	> ## STEP M — model loading
149	>
150	> **Tasks: M1, M2, M3, M4, M5. CLOSED.**
151	>
152	> Adding a task to this STEP requires opening STEP M+1 (with a DL/AD
153	> authorizing the new step) and placing the new tasks there.
154	
155	**Effect on INC-1**: `M-LR0a..M-LR7` could not be appended to STEP M.2
156	after-the-fact. They would require a new STEP (say, STEP M-LR) with its own
157	architecture authorization. The visibility of that new-STEP creation is the
158	gate — an operator or auditor reading the diff sees a structural edit, not a
159	cosmetic append.
160	
161	### SP-6 — Append-only spec amendments
162	
163	The core §1–§8 prose and the §6 entity table are **frozen** at each
164	architecture version. Subsequent changes land as a separate `§10 Amendments`
165	section carrying a datestamped delta. The entity table is a *computed* view:
166	its effective state at any moment is `§6 baseline` *overlaid with* `§10
167	amendments`, where overlays are explicitly diff-style, not in-place rewrites.
168	
169	**Closed form required** (example amendment block):
170	
171	```
172	§10.DL-n (YYYY-MM-DD)
173	  ADD §6.3 row: <Entity>(<fields>)
174	  ADD §6.7 row: <Composable>
175	  MODIFY §6.7 row: <ExistingComposable> — append <clause>
176	  MODIFY §6.6 row: <ExistingClass>        — append <clause>
177	```
178	
179	Baseline prose is not edited. Overlays are diff-reviewable.
180	
181	**Effect on INC-1**: The current DL-12 shape — prose in one place, in-place
182	entity-table edits at lines 1044/1126/1127 — would be refactored into a
183	single append-only block. Every amendment is visibly a delta, and the
184	baseline remains the reference point. Retroactive edits to earlier
185	entity-table rows become impossible. An auditor scrolling §6 sees the
186	*baseline* vocabulary; an auditor scrolling §10 sees every subsequent
187	adjustment in chronological order with full traceability.
188	
189	### SP-7 — Authorization citation on every row
190	
191	Each entity-table row carries an `Authorized-by:` field citing the AD or DL
192	that justifies its existence.
193	
194	**Closed form required** (adds a column):
195	
196	| Entity | Type | File:line | Role | Key signatures / fields | **Authorized by** |
197	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
198	| `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | `…:60` | Loader state | `Idle, Loading, Ready, Error` | AD-8 (original) + AD-17 (if Downloading promoted) |
199	| `LlmStatusIndicator` | composable | `…:1` | … | … | **MISSING — CI FAIL** |
200	
201	CI parses the `Authorized-by` column and verifies every citation resolves to
202	an AD/DL that exists and has operator approval. Orphan citations fail.
203	
204	**Effect on INC-1**: `LlmStatusIndicator`'s row could not be added without
205	citing an authorizing AD. DL-12 alone would not qualify (per SP-3). The row
206	remains un-addable until AD-17 exists and is approved.
207	
208	---
209	
210	## Composition — what the original spec would have looked like
211	
212	If SP-1 through SP-7 had been in place from project day one, the entire DL-12
213	work would have hit a wall at its very first step. A disciplined architect,
214	attempting to ship "non-blocking model load with progress bar", would have
215	been forced to:
216	
217	1. **Check the Phase I manifest (SP-2)** — see that progress-bar UX is not
218	   listed → halt.
219	2. **Open AD-17 candidate** — write full AD with alternatives (block on load
220	   / spinner / progress bar / defer to Phase II), choice, rationale.
221	3. **Seek operator approval on phase promotion (SP-2 + SP-3)** — operator
222	   decides whether to promote or defer.
223	4. **If promoted**: update the Phase I manifest, unlock the closed-set
224	   additions (SP-1) for `LlmServiceState`, write the amendment block (SP-6)
225	   with all entity-table overlays, add the `Authorized-by: AD-17` column
226	   entries (SP-7), open a new `CHECKLIST.md` STEP with its closed task list
227	   (SP-5).
228	5. **Only then**: a coder executes the now-authorized checklist tasks and
229	   produces the code.
230	
231	Total architect attention to reach step 5: roughly two hours — less than half
232	what the chaotic DL-12 drift cost in practice — and the output is an
233	authorized spec + authorized tree with zero contamination.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## Tradeoff — honest counter-argument
238	
239	Closed specs trade **ceremony for correctness**. They are strictly more
240	annoying to write. The cost is borne by architects; the benefit is borne by
241	everyone else on the project, especially parallel coders and future auditors.
242	
243	The honest counter-argument: closed specs can become an impediment during
244	early exploration, when the right shape is genuinely not yet known. Forcing
245	closure on a spec that is still being discovered produces premature
246	abstraction and false-precision rows that later need to be rewritten, which
247	itself violates I1 (Rugpull Defence — no taping over your own mistakes).
248	
249	**Resolution**: closure is a **phase gate**, not a permanent state.
250	
251	- An early-exploration project uses **permissive specs**. Entity-table rows
252	  are aspirational; the feature manifest is a wishlist; DLs carry speculative
253	  decisions. This is the correct mode before Phase I is declared shippable.
254	- At the moment a Phase is declared "shippable" (operator-authored milestone
255	  in `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`), that Phase's manifest and entity table **close**
256	  per SP-1..SP-7.
257	- Later phases **reopen**, architect, close again. The reopen is a
258	  first-class event with its own AD.
259	
260	This matches I1's "pull the rug yourself early" stance: each phase-closure is
261	the operator deliberately pulling the rug on further in-place amendment, so
262	that later "simple fixes" are *structurally forced* to be first-class
263	phase-boundary edits rather than silent drift.
264	
265	The incident at INC-1 is an artifact of DeepScriber leaving its Phase I specs
266	permissive past the point where Phase I was declared shippable. The remedy,
267	going forward, is to apply SP-1..SP-7 at the moment any phase is declared
268	shippable, and to never retroactively open a closed phase.
269	
270	---
271	
272	## Applied — adoption checklist
273	
274	A project adopts SC1 via the following ordered edits. Each step is
275	reversible; the full set is testable by running the proposed CI rules against
276	the pre- and post-adoption spec.
277	
278	1. **Audit existing enumerations** (entity-table sealed classes + enums).
279	   For each row, append `**Closed set, Phase <N>:**` and list the exact
280	   variants. If the set is under active negotiation, mark it `**Open —
281	   discovery:**` with a target close date.
282	
283	2. **Add `§1.5 Phase I Feature Manifest (CLOSED)`** to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
284	   Enumerate every user- and developer-visible feature in Phase I. Any
285	   ambiguous item is resolved (promoted or deferred) before declaring
286	   closure.
287	
288	3. **Add an `Authorized-by` column** to every §6.x entity-table. Retroactively
289	   populate from the commit history or known AD/DL that introduced each row.
290	   Rows that cannot be traced are either (a) moved to an `§6.0 Orphans`
291	   section for retrospective authorization or (b) deleted if the code they
292	   describe is also to be deleted.
293	
294	4. **Add the orphan-check + stranded-check CI rule** (SP-4) to the project's
295	   CI config (e.g., `.forgejo/workflows/build.yaml` or `.github/workflows/*`).
296	   The first CI run surfaces all existing orphans; resolve each via (a)
297	   adding a row, (b) deleting the file, or (c) moving to `§6.0 Orphans` for
298	   explicit retrospective handling.
299	
300	5. **Declare every existing `CHECKLIST.md` STEP closed**, by appending
301	   `**CLOSED.**` after its task list. STEPs still in flux remain open and
302	   are explicitly marked `**Open — STEP <N> not yet closed.**`.
303	
304	6. **Rewrite any in-place §6 entity-table edits since Phase I declaration**
305	   as `§10 Amendments` (SP-6). This is the most invasive step; it may be
306	   deferred to a natural refactor moment if the current in-place edits are
307	   few.
308	
309	7. **Add an AD to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`** declaring adoption of SC1 from
310	   version `<X>` forward, citing this file.
311	
312	8. **Add a one-line reference in the project's `CLAUDE.md`**:
313	
314	   ```markdown
315	   ## Spec conventions
316	   - Adopts `~/forgejo/admin/DOCS/SPEC_CONVENTIONS/closed-spec-properties.md`
317	     (SC1) as of version <X>.
318	   ```
319	
320	After these eight edits, every future DL-12-style drift is structurally
321	refused at one of the seven closure gates. The agent does not need to
322	remember ETHOS-7 or the ARCHITECT → TRANSFORM → APPROVE → EXECUTE sequence —
323	the spec's own shape makes that sequence the only path forward.
324	
325	---
326	
327	## Cross-references
328	
329	- **Ideology upstream**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation) +
330	  I1 (Rugpull Defence — rug-pull via phase closure is the engineering form of
331	  I1).
332	- **Precipitating evidence**: `INCIDENTS/simple-fix-contamination.md` —
333	  forensic table + classes (A/B) + five-label taxonomy.
334	- **Global rule consequence**: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-1..I-6. SC1 does not
335	  replace those rules; it makes them enforceable at spec-shape level rather
336	  than agent-behaviour level.
337	- **Tooling**: `TOOLING_CONVENTIONS.md` — the CI rules from SP-4 and SP-7 are
338	  concrete tooling and should be cross-referenced there once implemented.

# SC1 — Closed Spec Properties (SP-1..SP-7)

- **Version**: 1.0
- **Date**: 2026-05-04
- **Status**: Proposal
- **Precipitating incident(s)**: [INC-1 — The Simple-Fix Contamination](../INCIDENTS/simple-fix-contamination.md)
- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation)
- **Applies to**: every project that has declared a shippable phase (Phase I or later)

---

## Problem statement

Permissive specs admit drift additively. An agent (or operator) who wants to
add a feature, a sealed-class variant, a composable, or a checklist task can do
so by *appending* to the existing `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` + `CHECKLIST.md` —
even when the addition materially changes Phase scope or entity-table shape.

The result is **retroactive legitimization**: the spec grows to match whatever
code shipped, rather than constraining what the code may ship. The single
source of truth becomes a scribe of the tree, not a governor of it.

The incident at `INC-1` traces one concrete occurrence: a "simple add a
progress bar" ask produced ~700 lines of DL prose, in-place entity-table
edits, a new composable, a new screen, and seven checklist tasks — all
admitted additively, none stopped by the existing spec's own shape. The
current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` global rules (I-1 through I-6) describe the
correct workflow but rely on agent discipline to enforce it. Agent discipline
is insufficient; the drift fires at exactly the moments when the agent's
immediate "helpfulness" instinct is strongest and discipline is weakest.

This convention **moves enforcement from agent behaviour to spec shape**. A
closed spec refuses the drift at write time. The agent does not need to
remember the sequence; the sequence is the only path the spec permits.

---

## The seven properties

Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the closed
form required, (c) the structural effect on `INC-1`.

### SP-1 — Closed-set declarations on every enumeration

Every sealed class, enum, or finite variant set in the entity table must carry
an explicit closure marker naming the Phase at which it was closed.

**Permissive form** (currently allowed in DeepScriber `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`
§6.3 line 1044):

> `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | … | `Idle, Downloading(...), Loading, Ready, Error(message)` (per DL-12 — `Downloading` variant added …)

**Closed form required**:

> `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | … | **Closed set, Phase I:** `Idle, Loading, Ready, Error(message)`. Addition of a variant is a Phase boundary event and requires a new AD (not a DL).

**Effect on INC-1**: Adding `Downloading` would not be a DL-level edit; it
would require either a new AD (alternatives/choice/rationale round, operator
approval) or Phase II deferral. The "just add a variant" path does not exist.

### SP-2 — Phase scope enumerated and closed

`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md §1` or a new `§1.5 Phase I Feature Manifest` must
enumerate the **exact** set of user-visible and developer-visible features in
Phase I, and declare it **CLOSED**.

**Closed form required**:

> **Phase I feature manifest (CLOSED):**
> 1. Audio capture + VAD chunking
> 2. On-device transcription (engine per AD-n)
> 3. Phase I tools (count per AD-10)
> 4. Two-pass inference (per AD-5)
> 5. Post-recording diarization (per AD-3)
> 6. Session history + annotation editing
> 7. KB ingestion (path per AD-15)
> 8. Entitlement gating
>
> Any feature not in this list is Phase II or later. Lifting a feature from
> Phase II to Phase I requires a new AD *and* a documented phase-boundary
> review, not a DL.

**Effect on INC-1**: The line in DL-12 — *"lifted from 'Phase II refinement'
to Phase I scope"* — would fail the phase-boundary gate. The progress-bar UX
would remain Phase II until a proper AD promoted it.

### SP-3 — DL authority is bounded; DLs cannot change scope

DLs (Decision Log entries) are explicitly **post-AD clarifications**, not
alternatives to ADs. Their charter:

> A DL resolves an ambiguity, contradiction, or wave-2 halt *within* the
> existing AD + entity-table envelope. A DL cannot:
> - Add a variant to a closed set (SP-1).
> - Add a feature to a closed phase manifest (SP-2).
> - Add an entity-table row that no AD authorizes (SP-7).
> - Promote scope from a later phase to the current phase (SP-2).
>
> Any DL that attempts the above must be promoted to an AD (with alternatives,
> choice, rationale, operator approval) before it can land.

**Effect on INC-1**: DL-12 performs all four forbidden operations. It adds a
variant (`Downloading`), adds features (non-blocking load + progress UI +
gating matrix), adds entity-table rows (`LlmStatusIndicator`), and promotes
scope. Under SP-3 it is rejected at write time and must be rewritten as AD-17
with the full authorization round.

### SP-4 — Entity-table completeness gate (CI-enforced)

A CI check verifies that every source file in the tracked language(s) has
exactly one `File:line` citation in the entity table, and every entity-table
`File:line` citation points at a file that exists.

**CI rule (example for a Kotlin project)**:

```bash
# Orphan check: files in tree with no entity-table citation
comm -23 \
  <(git ls-files '*.kt' | sort -u) \
  <(grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z/._-]+\.kt:[0-9]+`' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md \
    | sed 's/:[0-9]*`$//; s/^`//' \
    | sort -u) \
  | grep . && { echo "ORPHAN FILES — every .kt file must have a §6 entity-table row"; exit 1; }

# Stranded check: citations with no file
comm -13 \
  <(git ls-files '*.kt' | sort -u) \
  <(grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z/._-]+\.kt:[0-9]+`' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md \
    | sed 's/:[0-9]*`$//; s/^`//' \
    | sort -u) \
  | grep . && { echo "STRANDED CITATIONS — entity-table row points at non-existent file"; exit 1; }
```

Adapt the glob pattern and citation regex per project language. The invariant
is **1:1 correspondence** between tracked-source files and entity-table
citations.

**Effect on INC-1**: `SplashScreen.kt` could not be committed, because CI
would report it as an orphan (no §6.7 row). The Class B contamination (as
classified in INC-1) becomes structurally impossible.

### SP-5 — Checklist STEP closure

Each STEP in `CHECKLIST.md` declares its task inventory as closed:

**Closed form required**:

> ## STEP M — model loading
>
> **Tasks: M1, M2, M3, M4, M5. CLOSED.**
>
> Adding a task to this STEP requires opening STEP M+1 (with a DL/AD
> authorizing the new step) and placing the new tasks there.

**Effect on INC-1**: `M-LR0a..M-LR7` could not be appended to STEP M.2
after-the-fact. They would require a new STEP (say, STEP M-LR) with its own
architecture authorization. The visibility of that new-STEP creation is the
gate — an operator or auditor reading the diff sees a structural edit, not a
cosmetic append.

### SP-6 — Append-only spec amendments

The core §1–§8 prose and the §6 entity table are **frozen** at each
architecture version. Subsequent changes land as a separate `§10 Amendments`
section carrying a datestamped delta. The entity table is a *computed* view:
its effective state at any moment is `§6 baseline` *overlaid with* `§10
amendments`, where overlays are explicitly diff-style, not in-place rewrites.

**Closed form required** (example amendment block):

```
§10.DL-n (YYYY-MM-DD)
  ADD §6.3 row: <Entity>(<fields>)
  ADD §6.7 row: <Composable>
  MODIFY §6.7 row: <ExistingComposable> — append <clause>
  MODIFY §6.6 row: <ExistingClass>        — append <clause>
```

Baseline prose is not edited. Overlays are diff-reviewable.

**Effect on INC-1**: The current DL-12 shape — prose in one place, in-place
entity-table edits at lines 1044/1126/1127 — would be refactored into a
single append-only block. Every amendment is visibly a delta, and the
baseline remains the reference point. Retroactive edits to earlier
entity-table rows become impossible. An auditor scrolling §6 sees the
*baseline* vocabulary; an auditor scrolling §10 sees every subsequent
adjustment in chronological order with full traceability.

### SP-7 — Authorization citation on every row

Each entity-table row carries an `Authorized-by:` field citing the AD or DL
that justifies its existence.

**Closed form required** (adds a column):

| Entity | Type | File:line | Role | Key signatures / fields | **Authorized by** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | `…:60` | Loader state | `Idle, Loading, Ready, Error` | AD-8 (original) + AD-17 (if Downloading promoted) |
| `LlmStatusIndicator` | composable | `…:1` | … | … | **MISSING — CI FAIL** |

CI parses the `Authorized-by` column and verifies every citation resolves to
an AD/DL that exists and has operator approval. Orphan citations fail.

**Effect on INC-1**: `LlmStatusIndicator`'s row could not be added without
citing an authorizing AD. DL-12 alone would not qualify (per SP-3). The row
remains un-addable until AD-17 exists and is approved.

---

## Composition — what the original spec would have looked like

If SP-1 through SP-7 had been in place from project day one, the entire DL-12
work would have hit a wall at its very first step. A disciplined architect,
attempting to ship "non-blocking model load with progress bar", would have
been forced to:

1. **Check the Phase I manifest (SP-2)** — see that progress-bar UX is not
   listed → halt.
2. **Open AD-17 candidate** — write full AD with alternatives (block on load
   / spinner / progress bar / defer to Phase II), choice, rationale.
3. **Seek operator approval on phase promotion (SP-2 + SP-3)** — operator
   decides whether to promote or defer.
4. **If promoted**: update the Phase I manifest, unlock the closed-set
   additions (SP-1) for `LlmServiceState`, write the amendment block (SP-6)
   with all entity-table overlays, add the `Authorized-by: AD-17` column
   entries (SP-7), open a new `CHECKLIST.md` STEP with its closed task list
   (SP-5).
5. **Only then**: a coder executes the now-authorized checklist tasks and
   produces the code.

Total architect attention to reach step 5: roughly two hours — less than half
what the chaotic DL-12 drift cost in practice — and the output is an
authorized spec + authorized tree with zero contamination.

---

## Tradeoff — honest counter-argument

Closed specs trade **ceremony for correctness**. They are strictly more
annoying to write. The cost is borne by architects; the benefit is borne by
everyone else on the project, especially parallel coders and future auditors.

The honest counter-argument: closed specs can become an impediment during
early exploration, when the right shape is genuinely not yet known. Forcing
closure on a spec that is still being discovered produces premature
abstraction and false-precision rows that later need to be rewritten, which
itself violates I1 (Rugpull Defence — no taping over your own mistakes).

**Resolution**: closure is a **phase gate**, not a permanent state.

- An early-exploration project uses **permissive specs**. Entity-table rows
  are aspirational; the feature manifest is a wishlist; DLs carry speculative
  decisions. This is the correct mode before Phase I is declared shippable.
- At the moment a Phase is declared "shippable" (operator-authored milestone
  in `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`), that Phase's manifest and entity table **close**
  per SP-1..SP-7.
- Later phases **reopen**, architect, close again. The reopen is a
  first-class event with its own AD.

This matches I1's "pull the rug yourself early" stance: each phase-closure is
the operator deliberately pulling the rug on further in-place amendment, so
that later "simple fixes" are *structurally forced* to be first-class
phase-boundary edits rather than silent drift.

The incident at INC-1 is an artifact of DeepScriber leaving its Phase I specs
permissive past the point where Phase I was declared shippable. The remedy,
going forward, is to apply SP-1..SP-7 at the moment any phase is declared
shippable, and to never retroactively open a closed phase.

---

## Applied — adoption checklist

A project adopts SC1 via the following ordered edits. Each step is
reversible; the full set is testable by running the proposed CI rules against
the pre- and post-adoption spec.

1. **Audit existing enumerations** (entity-table sealed classes + enums).
   For each row, append `**Closed set, Phase <N>:**` and list the exact
   variants. If the set is under active negotiation, mark it `**Open —
   discovery:**` with a target close date.

2. **Add `§1.5 Phase I Feature Manifest (CLOSED)`** to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
   Enumerate every user- and developer-visible feature in Phase I. Any
   ambiguous item is resolved (promoted or deferred) before declaring
   closure.

3. **Add an `Authorized-by` column** to every §6.x entity-table. Retroactively
   populate from the commit history or known AD/DL that introduced each row.
   Rows that cannot be traced are either (a) moved to an `§6.0 Orphans`
   section for retrospective authorization or (b) deleted if the code they
   describe is also to be deleted.

4. **Add the orphan-check + stranded-check CI rule** (SP-4) to the project's
   CI config (e.g., `.forgejo/workflows/build.yaml` or `.github/workflows/*`).
   The first CI run surfaces all existing orphans; resolve each via (a)
   adding a row, (b) deleting the file, or (c) moving to `§6.0 Orphans` for
   explicit retrospective handling.

5. **Declare every existing `CHECKLIST.md` STEP closed**, by appending
   `**CLOSED.**` after its task list. STEPs still in flux remain open and

   few.

7. **Add an AD to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`** declaring adoption of SC1 from
   version `<X>` forward, citing this file.

8. **Add a one-line reference in the project's `CLAUDE.md`**:

   ```markdown
   ## Spec conventions
   - Adopts `~/forgejo/admin/DOCS/SPEC_CONVENTIONS/closed-spec-properties.md`
     (SC1) as of version <X>.
   ```

After these eight edits, every future DL-12-style drift is structurally
refused at one of the seven closure gates. The agent does not need to
remember ETHOS-7 or the ARCHITECT → TRANSFORM → APPROVE → EXECUTE sequence —
the spec's own shape makes that sequence the only path forward.

---

- **Ideology upstream**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation) +
  I1 (Rugpull Defence — rug-pull via phase closure is the engineering form of
  I1).
- **Precipitating evidence**: `INCIDENTS/simple-fix-contamination.md` —
  forensic table + classes (A/B) + five-label taxonomy.
- **Global rule consequence**: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-1..I-6. SC1 does not
  replace those rules; it makes them enforceable at spec-shape level rather
  than agent-behaviour level.
- **Tooling**: `TOOLING_CONVENTIONS.md` — the CI rules from SP-4 and SP-7 are
  concrete tooling and should be cross-referenced there once implemented.

1	# SC1 — Closed Spec Properties (SP-1..SP-7)
2	
3	- **Version**: 1.0
4	- **Date**: 2026-05-04
5	- **Status**: Proposal
6	- **Precipitating incident(s)**: [INC-1 — The Simple-Fix Contamination](../INCIDENTS/simple-fix-contamination.md)
7	- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation)
8	- **Applies to**: every project that has declared a shippable phase (Phase I or later)
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Problem statement
13	
14	Permissive specs admit drift additively. An agent (or operator) who wants to
15	add a feature, a sealed-class variant, a composable, or a checklist task can do
16	so by *appending* to the existing `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` + `CHECKLIST.md` —
17	even when the addition materially changes Phase scope or entity-table shape.
18	
19	The result is **retroactive legitimization**: the spec grows to match whatever
20	code shipped, rather than constraining what the code may ship. The single
21	source of truth becomes a scribe of the tree, not a governor of it.
22	
23	The incident at `INC-1` traces one concrete occurrence: a "simple add a
24	progress bar" ask produced ~700 lines of DL prose, in-place entity-table
25	edits, a new composable, a new screen, and seven checklist tasks — all
26	admitted additively, none stopped by the existing spec's own shape. The
27	current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` global rules (I-1 through I-6) describe the
28	correct workflow but rely on agent discipline to enforce it. Agent discipline
29	is insufficient; the drift fires at exactly the moments when the agent's
30	immediate "helpfulness" instinct is strongest and discipline is weakest.
31	
32	This convention **moves enforcement from agent behaviour to spec shape**. A
33	closed spec refuses the drift at write time. The agent does not need to
34	remember the sequence; the sequence is the only path the spec permits.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## The seven properties
39	
40	Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the closed
41	form required, (c) the structural effect on `INC-1`.
42	
43	### SP-1 — Closed-set declarations on every enumeration
44	
45	Every sealed class, enum, or finite variant set in the entity table must carry
46	an explicit closure marker naming the Phase at which it was closed.
47	
48	**Permissive form** (currently allowed in DeepScriber `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`
49	§6.3 line 1044):
50	
51	> `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | … | `Idle, Downloading(...), Loading, Ready, Error(message)` (per DL-12 — `Downloading` variant added …)
52	
53	**Closed form required**:
54	
55	> `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | … | **Closed set, Phase I:** `Idle, Loading, Ready, Error(message)`. Addition of a variant is a Phase boundary event and requires a new AD (not a DL).
56	
57	**Effect on INC-1**: Adding `Downloading` would not be a DL-level edit; it
58	would require either a new AD (alternatives/choice/rationale round, operator
59	approval) or Phase II deferral. The "just add a variant" path does not exist.
60	
61	### SP-2 — Phase scope enumerated and closed
62	
63	`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md §1` or a new `§1.5 Phase I Feature Manifest` must
64	enumerate the **exact** set of user-visible and developer-visible features in
65	Phase I, and declare it **CLOSED**.
66	
67	**Closed form required**:
68	
69	> **Phase I feature manifest (CLOSED):**
70	> 1. Audio capture + VAD chunking
71	> 2. On-device transcription (engine per AD-n)
72	> 3. Phase I tools (count per AD-10)
73	> 4. Two-pass inference (per AD-5)
74	> 5. Post-recording diarization (per AD-3)
75	> 6. Session history + annotation editing
76	> 7. KB ingestion (path per AD-15)
77	> 8. Entitlement gating
78	>
79	> Any feature not in this list is Phase II or later. Lifting a feature from
80	> Phase II to Phase I requires a new AD *and* a documented phase-boundary
81	> review, not a DL.
82	
83	**Effect on INC-1**: The line in DL-12 — *"lifted from 'Phase II refinement'
84	to Phase I scope"* — would fail the phase-boundary gate. The progress-bar UX
85	would remain Phase II until a proper AD promoted it.
86	
87	### SP-3 — DL authority is bounded; DLs cannot change scope
88	
89	DLs (Decision Log entries) are explicitly **post-AD clarifications**, not
90	alternatives to ADs. Their charter:
91	
92	> A DL resolves an ambiguity, contradiction, or wave-2 halt *within* the
93	> existing AD + entity-table envelope. A DL cannot:
94	> - Add a variant to a closed set (SP-1).
95	> - Add a feature to a closed phase manifest (SP-2).
96	> - Add an entity-table row that no AD authorizes (SP-7).
97	> - Promote scope from a later phase to the current phase (SP-2).
98	>
99	> Any DL that attempts the above must be promoted to an AD (with alternatives,
100	> choice, rationale, operator approval) before it can land.
101	
102	**Effect on INC-1**: DL-12 performs all four forbidden operations. It adds a
103	variant (`Downloading`), adds features (non-blocking load + progress UI +
104	gating matrix), adds entity-table rows (`LlmStatusIndicator`), and promotes
105	scope. Under SP-3 it is rejected at write time and must be rewritten as AD-17
106	with the full authorization round.
107	
108	### SP-4 — Entity-table completeness gate (CI-enforced)
109	
110	A CI check verifies that every source file in the tracked language(s) has
111	exactly one `File:line` citation in the entity table, and every entity-table
112	`File:line` citation points at a file that exists.
113	
114	**CI rule (example for a Kotlin project)**:
115	
116	```bash
117	# Orphan check: files in tree with no entity-table citation
118	comm -23 \
119	  <(git ls-files '*.kt' | sort -u) \
120	  <(grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z/._-]+\.kt:[0-9]+`' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md \
121	    | sed 's/:[0-9]*`$//; s/^`//' \
122	    | sort -u) \
123	  | grep . && { echo "ORPHAN FILES — every .kt file must have a §6 entity-table row"; exit 1; }
124	
125	# Stranded check: citations with no file
126	comm -13 \
127	  <(git ls-files '*.kt' | sort -u) \
128	  <(grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z/._-]+\.kt:[0-9]+`' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md \
129	    | sed 's/:[0-9]*`$//; s/^`//' \
130	    | sort -u) \
131	  | grep . && { echo "STRANDED CITATIONS — entity-table row points at non-existent file"; exit 1; }
132	```
133	
134	Adapt the glob pattern and citation regex per project language. The invariant
135	is **1:1 correspondence** between tracked-source files and entity-table
136	citations.
137	
138	**Effect on INC-1**: `SplashScreen.kt` could not be committed, because CI
139	would report it as an orphan (no §6.7 row). The Class B contamination (as
140	classified in INC-1) becomes structurally impossible.
141	
142	### SP-5 — Checklist STEP closure
143	
144	Each STEP in `CHECKLIST.md` declares its task inventory as closed:
145	
146	**Closed form required**:
147	
148	> ## STEP M — model loading
149	>
150	> **Tasks: M1, M2, M3, M4, M5. CLOSED.**
151	>
152	> Adding a task to this STEP requires opening STEP M+1 (with a DL/AD
153	> authorizing the new step) and placing the new tasks there.
154	
155	**Effect on INC-1**: `M-LR0a..M-LR7` could not be appended to STEP M.2
156	after-the-fact. They would require a new STEP (say, STEP M-LR) with its own
157	architecture authorization. The visibility of that new-STEP creation is the
158	gate — an operator or auditor reading the diff sees a structural edit, not a
159	cosmetic append.
160	
161	### SP-6 — Append-only spec amendments
162	
163	The core §1–§8 prose and the §6 entity table are **frozen** at each
164	architecture version. Subsequent changes land as a separate `§10 Amendments`
165	section carrying a datestamped delta. The entity table is a *computed* view:
166	its effective state at any moment is `§6 baseline` *overlaid with* `§10
167	amendments`, where overlays are explicitly diff-style, not in-place rewrites.
168	
169	**Closed form required** (example amendment block):
170	
171	```
172	§10.DL-n (YYYY-MM-DD)
173	  ADD §6.3 row: <Entity>(<fields>)
174	  ADD §6.7 row: <Composable>
175	  MODIFY §6.7 row: <ExistingComposable> — append <clause>
176	  MODIFY §6.6 row: <ExistingClass>        — append <clause>
177	```
178	
179	Baseline prose is not edited. Overlays are diff-reviewable.
180	
181	**Effect on INC-1**: The current DL-12 shape — prose in one place, in-place
182	entity-table edits at lines 1044/1126/1127 — would be refactored into a
183	single append-only block. Every amendment is visibly a delta, and the
184	baseline remains the reference point. Retroactive edits to earlier
185	entity-table rows become impossible. An auditor scrolling §6 sees the
186	*baseline* vocabulary; an auditor scrolling §10 sees every subsequent
187	adjustment in chronological order with full traceability.
188	
189	### SP-7 — Authorization citation on every row
190	
191	Each entity-table row carries an `Authorized-by:` field citing the AD or DL
192	that justifies its existence.
193	
194	**Closed form required** (adds a column):
195	
196	| Entity | Type | File:line | Role | Key signatures / fields | **Authorized by** |
197	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
198	| `LlmServiceState` | sealed class | `…:60` | Loader state | `Idle, Loading, Ready, Error` | AD-8 (original) + AD-17 (if Downloading promoted) |
199	| `LlmStatusIndicator` | composable | `…:1` | … | … | **MISSING — CI FAIL** |
200	
201	CI parses the `Authorized-by` column and verifies every citation resolves to
202	an AD/DL that exists and has operator approval. Orphan citations fail.
203	
204	**Effect on INC-1**: `LlmStatusIndicator`'s row could not be added without
205	citing an authorizing AD. DL-12 alone would not qualify (per SP-3). The row
206	remains un-addable until AD-17 exists and is approved.
207	
208	---
209	
210	## Composition — what the original spec would have looked like
211	
212	If SP-1 through SP-7 had been in place from project day one, the entire DL-12
213	work would have hit a wall at its very first step. A disciplined architect,
214	attempting to ship "non-blocking model load with progress bar", would have
215	been forced to:
216	
217	1. **Check the Phase I manifest (SP-2)** — see that progress-bar UX is not
218	   listed → halt.
219	2. **Open AD-17 candidate** — write full AD with alternatives (block on load
220	   / spinner / progress bar / defer to Phase II), choice, rationale.
221	3. **Seek operator approval on phase promotion (SP-2 + SP-3)** — operator
222	   decides whether to promote or defer.
223	4. **If promoted**: update the Phase I manifest, unlock the closed-set
224	   additions (SP-1) for `LlmServiceState`, write the amendment block (SP-6)
225	   with all entity-table overlays, add the `Authorized-by: AD-17` column
226	   entries (SP-7), open a new `CHECKLIST.md` STEP with its closed task list
227	   (SP-5).
228	5. **Only then**: a coder executes the now-authorized checklist tasks and
229	   produces the code.
230	
231	Total architect attention to reach step 5: roughly two hours — less than half
232	what the chaotic DL-12 drift cost in practice — and the output is an
233	authorized spec + authorized tree with zero contamination.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## Tradeoff — honest counter-argument
238	
239	Closed specs trade **ceremony for correctness**. They are strictly more
240	annoying to write. The cost is borne by architects; the benefit is borne by
241	everyone else on the project, especially parallel coders and future auditors.
242	
243	The honest counter-argument: closed specs can become an impediment during
244	early exploration, when the right shape is genuinely not yet known. Forcing
245	closure on a spec that is still being discovered produces premature
246	abstraction and false-precision rows that later need to be rewritten, which
247	itself violates I1 (Rugpull Defence — no taping over your own mistakes).
248	
249	**Resolution**: closure is a **phase gate**, not a permanent state.
250	
251	- An early-exploration project uses **permissive specs**. Entity-table rows
252	  are aspirational; the feature manifest is a wishlist; DLs carry speculative
253	  decisions. This is the correct mode before Phase I is declared shippable.
254	- At the moment a Phase is declared "shippable" (operator-authored milestone
255	  in `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`), that Phase's manifest and entity table **close**
256	  per SP-1..SP-7.
257	- Later phases **reopen**, architect, close again. The reopen is a
258	  first-class event with its own AD.
259	
260	This matches I1's "pull the rug yourself early" stance: each phase-closure is
261	the operator deliberately pulling the rug on further in-place amendment, so
262	that later "simple fixes" are *structurally forced* to be first-class
263	phase-boundary edits rather than silent drift.
264	
265	The incident at INC-1 is an artifact of DeepScriber leaving its Phase I specs
266	permissive past the point where Phase I was declared shippable. The remedy,
267	going forward, is to apply SP-1..SP-7 at the moment any phase is declared
268	shippable, and to never retroactively open a closed phase.
269	
270	---
271	
272	## Applied — adoption checklist
273	
274	A project adopts SC1 via the following ordered edits. Each step is
275	reversible; the full set is testable by running the proposed CI rules against
276	the pre- and post-adoption spec.
277	
278	1. **Audit existing enumerations** (entity-table sealed classes + enums).
279	   For each row, append `**Closed set, Phase <N>:**` and list the exact
280	   variants. If the set is under active negotiation, mark it `**Open —
281	   discovery:**` with a target close date.
282	
283	2. **Add `§1.5 Phase I Feature Manifest (CLOSED)`** to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
284	   Enumerate every user- and developer-visible feature in Phase I. Any
285	   ambiguous item is resolved (promoted or deferred) before declaring
286	   closure.
287	
288	3. **Add an `Authorized-by` column** to every §6.x entity-table. Retroactively
289	   populate from the commit history or known AD/DL that introduced each row.
290	   Rows that cannot be traced are either (a) moved to an `§6.0 Orphans`
291	   section for retrospective authorization or (b) deleted if the code they
292	   describe is also to be deleted.
293	
294	4. **Add the orphan-check + stranded-check CI rule** (SP-4) to the project's
295	   CI config (e.g., `.forgejo/workflows/build.yaml` or `.github/workflows/*`).
296	   The first CI run surfaces all existing orphans; resolve each via (a)
297	   adding a row, (b) deleting the file, or (c) moving to `§6.0 Orphans` for
298	   explicit retrospective handling.
299	
300	5. **Declare every existing `CHECKLIST.md` STEP closed**, by appending
301	   `**CLOSED.**` after its task list. STEPs still in flux remain open and
302	   are explicitly marked `**Open — STEP <N> not yet closed.**`.
303

2	
3	- **Version**: 1.0
4	- **Date**: 2026-05-06
5	- **Status**: Adopted (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-7 landed 2026-05-06)
6	- **Precipitating incident(s)**: [INC-2 — The Swarm-Blocker Accept Clauses](../INCIDENTS/swarm-blocker-accept-clauses.md)
7	- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation)
8	- **Companion to**: SC1 (Closed Spec Properties); SC1 closes the *shape* a spec must take, SC2 closes the *shape* a CHECKLIST `Accept` clause must take; SC4 (Final Test Rubric / Gauntlet) closes the *shape* of the post-CODE runtime gauntlet — SC2's tradeoff punts runtime certification to SC4
9	- **Applies to**: every project that uses the four-phase MAP→ARCHITECT→PLAN→CODE workflow with a `CHECKLIST.md` contract
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Problem statement
14	
15	`CHECKLIST.md` is the contract for CODE-phase execution. Each task carries
16	`Files`/`Do`/`Verify`/`Accept` fields; coders read the contract, perform
17	`Do`, run `Verify`, observe `Accept`, and flip the marker.
18	
19	The canonical **four-stage marker discipline** is:
20	
21	> `[ ]` Task → `[/]` Undertaken Task → `[X]` Completed Task → `✅` Orchestrator-semantically-validated-as-complete Task
22	
23	`[ ]` is a one-coder-one-task-capable logical execution block formulated by an
24	architect (the sum-total of `[ ]` tasks comprises the assembly of
25	`ARCHITECTURE.md`); `[/]` is flipped by the assigned coder to acknowledge
26	Orchestrator assignment (task line suffixed with the coder session id where
27	possible); `[X]` is flipped by the coder on completion; `✅` is flipped only by
28	the Orchestrator upon semantic validation of the logical group of tasks. **The
29	logic: each of Orchestrator, Architect, Coder assigns work to a group other
30	than itself to execute, and each's work is checked by other than itself** —
31	assignment, execution, and validation are always separated across roles (I-12
32	generalized; provenance ledgered per step in the Postgres `task_ledger`).
33	
34	The discipline's original three-stage statement (`[ ]` → `[X]` → `✅`, with
35	`✅` only after `Verify` runs and matches `Accept`) was designed for sequential
36	single-coder execution. It treats the Accept clause as **a single-shot
37	observation made at the moment the task lands**.
38	
39	Single-shot observation is necessary but not sufficient for **swarm
40	dispatch**. When 14 coders run in parallel, when a coder picks up a task on a
41	fresh clone where prior coders already landed the work, when an architect
42	cycle revisits a previously-✅'d task — the Accept clause is observed many
43	times across many starting states. If the clause's truth value depends on
44	*which* starting state is observed, the swarm halts on whichever observation
45	sees the inconsistent truth.
46	
47	INC-2 (2026-05-06) traces the concrete cost: seven anti-idempotent `Accept`
48	clauses in DeepScriber's CHECKLIST.md halted a swarm dispatch in eight
49	places. The same CHECKLIST after the seven clauses were rewritten to
50	idempotent end-state assertions ran 28 coder dispatches across 4 waves with
51	**zero halts**.
52	
53	The current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` invariants I-1..I-6 (pre-2026-05-06) do not
54	constrain the shape of an Accept clause. I-5 ("verify by running") is
55	consistent with `adb logcat` filters that depend on logcat ring-buffer state,
56	with `git status --short` reads that depend on working-tree dirtiness, with
57	manual UI taps. The gap is between "verify by running once" (the original
58	framing) and "verify by running idempotently from any starting state" (what
59	swarm dispatch requires).
60	
61	This convention closes that gap. An Accept clause that satisfies AP-1..AP-4
62	is **observably equivalent under any starting state including the
63	post-success state** — the property a swarm dispatch demands.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## The five properties
68	
69	Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the
70	closed form required, (c) the structural effect on `INC-2`.
71	
72	### AP-1 — Idempotent end-state assertion (the core property)
73	
74	Every `Accept` clause must observe **committed, durable end-state** rather
75	than transient intermediate state.
76	
77	**Permissive form** (currently allowed in DeepScriber `CHECKLIST.md` pre-DL-14):
78	
79	> **B3 Accept** (line 1791): app is visible on device, logcat shows Koin
80	> initialization with no `RuntimeException`
81	
82	**Closed form required**:
83	
84	> **B3 Accept** (post-DL-14 revision): `./gradlew :androidApp:compileDebugKotlin`
85	> reports `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; `grep -c 'single<'
86	> androidApp/src/main/kotlin/di/AppModule.kt` reports a positive integer.
87	
88	**Effect on INC-2**: A coder picking up B3 on a fresh clone, on a clone where
89	the work already landed, or after re-running the task five times, observes
90	the same Accept result every time. The original clause was observation-of-
91	ring-buffer; the closed clause is observation-of-committed-source. The first
92	ages; the second does not.
93	
94	### AP-2 — Forbidden anti-patterns
95	
96	The following Accept-clause shapes are **forbidden** in any swarm-
97	dispatchable CHECKLIST:
98	
99	1. **Transient state observation** — `adb logcat` ring buffer reads;
100	   `git status --short` working-tree dirtiness; HTTP responses from
101	   external services that may rate-limit, deauthenticate, or restructure
102	   without notice; `top` / `ps` snapshots.
103	2. **Operator-gated checks** — manual UI taps on a phone; "open browser
104	   and check"; "install APK on a connected device and observe"; visual
105	   inspection of any kind.
106	3. **Smoke tests that double-verify** — any task whose Accept clause
107	   re-asserts a property already covered by another task's per-task
108	   gate. Example: a "shared module compiles" gate at end-of-STEP when
109	   every individual STEP task already runs `./gradlew :shared:compileTask`
110	   itself.
111	4. **Anti-idempotent commit/release Do blocks** — `git add` + `git commit`
112	   as the entire Do block. Works the first time; fails (or produces an
113	   empty commit) every subsequent time. Replace with a commit-reachability
114	   assertion (see AP-3).
115	
116	**Effect on INC-2**: Each of the seven offending clauses falls into exactly
117	one of these four buckets. The taxonomy is exhaustive over the observed
118	failure cases and predictive over the as-yet-unobserved ones (e.g., a future
119	clause that polls a Slack webhook for a deploy notification would fail under
120	AP-2.1 as soon as it's drafted).
121	
122	### AP-3 — Allowed palette (idempotent end-state forms)
123	
124	The following Accept-clause shapes are **allowed**:
125	
126	1. **Compile gate** — `./gradlew <module>:compileTask` (or equivalent)
127	   ending in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. The compile output observes committed
128	   source; same source produces same output across runs.
129	2. **File presence + hash** — `ls -la <path>` for existence,
130	   `sha256sum <file>` for content fingerprint. Both observe committed
131	   filesystem state.
132	3. **Content match against committed source** — `grep -c '<exact pattern>'
133	   <committed file>`. The grep operates on tracked source; same source
134	   produces same count.
135	4. **Commit reachability** — `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}` (exact
136	   SHA) or `git log --oneline | grep '<message prefix>'` (message form,
137	   stable across rebase). Both observe immutable git history.
138	5. **Tracked-in-git assertion** — `git ls-files <path> | wc -l`. Reads
139	   committed state, not working-tree state. This is the idempotent
140	   replacement for `git status` working-tree checks.
141	6. **Attribute assertion** — `git check-attr filter <path>` etc. Reads
142	   committed `.gitattributes`, idempotent across re-runs.
143	
144	**Effect on INC-2**: Every one of the seven anti-idempotent clauses rewrote
145	into one or two members of this palette in 1-3 lines of CHECKLIST.md edit
146	each. The palette is the constructive complement to AP-2's forbidden list.
147	
148	### AP-4 — Operator verification protocol carve-out
149	
150	When runtime device verification is **genuinely required** — FGS-microphone
151	end-to-end on a connected device, on-device LLM cold-load progress UI
152	rendering correctly, recording lifecycle producing an on-disk session
153	directory — the verification is recorded as an **Operator verification
154	protocol** inside the relevant DL in `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, **not** as a
155	CHECKLIST task.
156	
157	**Permissive form** (allowed in DeepScriber pre-DL-14):
158	
159	> A DL prescribes a CHECKLIST task with `adb install`, `adb shell monkey`,
160	> `adb logcat`, manual button-tap, observation prose. The task lives on the
161	> swarm dispatch surface and halts the swarm whenever runtime verification
162	> can't run.
163	
164	**Closed form required**:
165	
166	> A DL prescribes the **architectural decision** (what the code looks like)
167	> and may prescribe **per-task BUILD SUCCESSFUL gates** as the swarm-side
168	> verification mechanism. Where runtime device walkthrough is genuinely
169	> required, the DL gains an `**Operator verification protocol**` sub-
170	> section listing the manual steps. This sub-section is documentation,
171	> not a swarm task.
172	
173	**Effect on INC-2**: DL-9 (FGS-microphone gating) and DL-12 (non-blocking
174	LLM load) in DeepScriber's `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` each gained an Operator
175	verification protocol sub-section in the same 2026-05-06 commit. The B3,
176	B4, M-LR6, M-VRY tasks they had spawned were either rewritten (B3) or
177	deleted from the swarm CHECKLIST (B4, M-LR6, M-VRY); the runtime walkthrough
178	they used to gate is now the operator's manual post-swarm check, recorded
179	in the DL where the architectural decision lives.
180	
181	### AP-5 — Coder→orchestrator success-report contract for position-sensitive output (DRAFT — not yet adopted)
182	
183	> **Status**: DRAFT, raised 2026-05-06, refined same-day. NOT YET adopted as
184	> doctrine — pending a dedicated architect cycle informed by a real
185	> position-sensitive coder dispatch where the rewrite-old-block pattern is
186	> provably insufficient.
187	
188	When a coder's `Do` block writes a **position-sensitive new block** (not an
189	edit-in-place that anchors to existing content), the resolved file:line of
190	the new block is sometimes data downstream tasks need to reference. Three
191	mechanisms were proposed initially:
192	
193	1. Interprocess file (`.checklist-lineno-handoff.json`).
194	2. CHECKLIST.md amendment with orchestrator's blessing.
195	3. Direct dispatch-return: coder emits resolved positions in stdout as part
196	   of its standard report.
197	
198	**Refinement (2026-05-06)**: Don't invent a new IPC channel. The current
199	coder-dispatch prompt template requires:
200	
201	> Report: CHECKLIST diff, Do/Verify output, any halt.
202	
203	Extend the requirement:
204	
205	> Report: CHECKLIST diff, Do/Verify output, any halt. **And any line numbers /
206	> anchor positions downstream tasks will need to reference, on successful
207	> completion as well as on halt.**
208	
209	Coder emits e.g. `RESOLVED: <task-id> → <file>:<line> [anchor=<name>]` as
210	part of its normal report. Orchestrator parses these out of stdout and
211	threads them into subsequent dispatch prompts. Mechanism (1) and (2) are
212	deprecated as over-engineered.
213	
214	**Edge cases dissolved by the refinement**: race between concurrent coders
215	writing IPC and orchestrator reading; stale-anchor cleanup discipline
216	(positions are never persisted on disk); detection of an anchor's
217	containing block being deleted (degrades to pure orchestrator-state
218	concern).
219	
220	**Edge cases that remain (the agenda for the architect cycle that promotes
221	AP-5 from DRAFT to adopted)**:
222	
223	1. Anchor naming collisions across concurrent coders — manageable by
224	   requiring anchors to include task-id, but not yet specified as a hard
225	   rule.
226	2. What happens when a coder's commented anchor becomes a later task's
227	   `old_string` Edit target — anchor strings need to be picked so they're
228	   not Edit-target candidates; pattern-design question.
229	3. Orchestrator's own state management — has to absorb reported positions
230	   into the next-wave dispatch prompts; needs an explicit pattern, not
231	   ad-hoc.
232	4. Empirical pressure: 2026-05-06's dispatch hit several "file modified
233	   since read" Edit-tool races on CHECKLIST.md when many parallel coders
234	   flipped markers simultaneously. Whether anchor-based content matching
235	   would help, or whether marker-flip atomicity is a separate concern.
236	
237	**Effect on INC-2**: Marked DRAFT, not adopted, but raised here so the
238	architect cycle that ratifies it has a concrete starting point. The
239	2026-05-06 swarm dispatch did not actually require AP-5 — every offending
240	clause was an Accept-clause shape (AP-1..AP-4), not a position-handoff
241	shape. AP-5 is forward-looking; AP-1..AP-4 are the load-bearing remediation
242	of INC-2.
243	
244	---
245	
246	## Tradeoff / honest counter-argument
247	
248	Closing every Accept clause to AP-3's palette removes **end-to-end runtime
249	verification** from the swarm dispatch surface. A naive reading would say
250	"now the swarm only verifies that the code compiles, not that it runs" —
251	and that's correct, in the sense that swarm-side verification covers
252	*structural* correctness (compile, content, commit reachability) and not
253	*behavioural* correctness (does the recording actually start, does the
254	permission dialog actually appear).
255	
256	The tradeoff is deliberate. Behavioural verification is **better** when it
257	runs as an Operator verification protocol than when it runs as a swarm task,
258	for two reasons:
259	
260	1. **Scope visibility**: a CHECKLIST task that says "tap Start, observe
261	   recording, tap Stop" hides from the operator that they will be tapping a
262	   button. They see a swarm complete, assume the work is done, and discover
263	   on next launch that nobody actually verified the runtime path. The
264	   Operator verification protocol carve-out (AP-4) makes the manual step
265	   explicit and visible.
266	
267	2. **Reliability under repetition**: an `adb logcat` filter that's
268	   expected to be empty 99% of the time tells the operator nothing on the
269	   1st run, the 10th run, or the 100th. A compile gate that fails when
270	   the code is wrong tells the operator something every time. The two
271	   verifications are complementary; collapsing them into one swarm task
272	   loses the complement.
273	
274	The cost of SC2 is that the CHECKLIST becomes incomplete *on its own* —
275	it does not, alone, certify that the project runs. It certifies that the
276	project compiles, that its files are present and tracked, that its commit
277	graph is intact. Runtime certification lives elsewhere (in the DL's
278	Operator verification protocol sub-section, in the operator's manual
279	post-swarm walkthrough, in CI integration tests when those exist). This
280	is the right shape for a swarm-dispatchable contract; a CHECKLIST that
281	tries to certify runtime as well as structure cannot be swarmed.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Applied (DeepScriber, 2026-05-06)
286	
287	DeepScriber adopted SC2 in commit `67a671d`. The mechanical edits were:
288	
289	1. **`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`** — new DL-14 codifying AP-1..AP-4 in DeepScriber-
290	   local language. DL-5 / DL-9 / DL-11 / DL-12 each had their procedural-
291	   verification clauses rewritten or deleted.
292	2. **`CHECKLIST.md`** — 7 deletions (L1, L2, B4, MM5b, M-LR6, M-VRY,
293	   T-1..T-6); 5 idempotent rewrites (B0a, B0d, B3, M-LRT4, M-LRT5);
294	   timestamped backup of the pre-refactor state preserved.
295	3. **Swarm validation** — 28 coder dispatches across 4 waves, 107 ✅, zero
296	   halts.
297	4. **Project memory** — `learning_idempotent_accept_clauses.md` +
298	   `feedback_no_diagnosing_in_code_mode.md` recorded in
299	   `~/.claude/projects/-home-robin-forgejo-DeepScriber/memory/`.
300	
301	For a project adopting SC2 fresh:
302	
303	1. Audit `CHECKLIST.md`: `grep -nE 'adb logcat|git status --short|tap '
304	   CHECKLIST.md` and similar; flag every match as a candidate for
305	   AP-1..AP-2 violation.
306	2. For each flagged task: rewrite using AP-3 palette, OR delete + replace
307	   with an Operator verification protocol entry in the DL where the
308	   architectural decision lives (AP-4).
309	3. Audit `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` DL entries: `grep -nE 'adb logcat|adb
310	   install|tap |observe in logcat' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` — flag every match
311	   as a DL prescribing an anti-idempotent gate.
312	4. For each flagged DL: revise the prescription to drop the procedural
313	   verification (keep the architectural decision); add an `**Operator
314	   verification protocol**` sub-section if runtime walkthrough is
315	   genuinely required.
316	5. Validate by attempting a swarm dispatch of all unfinished tasks. The
317	   adoption is complete when zero halts occur.
318	6. Record adoption in the project's `CLAUDE.md` (citing `SC2`) and add an
319	   AD entry to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` recording the convention adoption
320	   itself.
321	
322	---
323	
324	## Versioning
325	
326	- 1.0 (2026-05-06): Initial adoption. AP-1..AP-4 are load-bearing.
327	  AP-5 is DRAFT, awaiting architect-cycle ratification.
328

failure cases and predictive over the as-yet-unobserved ones (e.g., a future
clause that polls a Slack webhook for a deploy notification would fail under
AP-2.1 as soon as it's drafted).

### AP-3 — Allowed palette (idempotent end-state forms)

The following Accept-clause shapes are **allowed**:

1. **Compile gate** — `./gradlew <module>:compileTask` (or equivalent)
   ending in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. The compile output observes committed
   source; same source produces same output across runs.
2. **File presence + hash** — `ls -la <path>` for existence,
   `sha256sum <file>` for content fingerprint. Both observe committed
   filesystem state.
3. **Content match against committed source** — `grep -c '<exact pattern>'
   <committed file>`. The grep operates on tracked source; same source
   produces same count.
4. **Commit reachability** — `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}` (exact
   SHA) or `git log --oneline | grep '<message prefix>'` (message form,
   stable across rebase). Both observe immutable git history.
5. **Tracked-in-git assertion** — `git ls-files <path> | wc -l`. Reads
   committed state, not working-tree state. This is the idempotent
   replacement for `git status` working-tree checks.
6. **Attribute assertion** — `git check-attr filter <path>` etc. Reads
   committed `.gitattributes`, idempotent across re-runs.

**Effect on INC-2**: Every one of the seven anti-idempotent clauses rewrote
into one or two members of this palette in 1-3 lines of CHECKLIST.md edit
each. The palette is the constructive complement to AP-2's forbidden list.

### AP-4 — Operator verification protocol carve-out

When runtime device verification is **genuinely required** — FGS-microphone
end-to-end on a connected device, on-device LLM cold-load progress UI
rendering correctly, recording lifecycle producing an on-disk session
directory — the verification is recorded as an **Operator verification
protocol** inside the relevant DL in `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, **not** as a
CHECKLIST task.

**Permissive form** (allowed in DeepScriber pre-DL-14):

> A DL prescribes a CHECKLIST task with `adb install`, `adb shell monkey`,
> `adb logcat`, manual button-tap, observation prose. The task lives on the
> swarm dispatch surface and halts the swarm whenever runtime verification
> can't run.

**Closed form required**:

> A DL prescribes the **architectural decision** (what the code looks like)
> and may prescribe **per-task BUILD SUCCESSFUL gates** as the swarm-side
> verification mechanism. Where runtime device walkthrough is genuinely
> required, the DL gains an `**Operator verification protocol**` sub-
> section listing the manual steps. This sub-section is documentation,
> not a swarm task.

**Effect on INC-2**: DL-9 (FGS-microphone gating) and DL-12 (non-blocking
LLM load) in DeepScriber's `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` each gained an Operator
verification protocol sub-section in the same 2026-05-06 commit. The B3,
B4, M-LR6, M-VRY tasks they had spawned were either rewritten (B3) or
deleted from the swarm CHECKLIST (B4, M-LR6, M-VRY); the runtime walkthrough
they used to gate is now the operator's manual post-swarm check, recorded
in the DL where the architectural decision lives.

### AP-5 — Coder→orchestrator success-report contract for position-sensitive output (DRAFT — not yet adopted)

> **Status**: DRAFT, raised 2026-05-06, refined same-day. NOT YET adopted as
> doctrine — pending a dedicated architect cycle informed by a real
> position-sensitive coder dispatch where the rewrite-old-block pattern is
> provably insufficient.

When a coder's `Do` block writes a **position-sensitive new block** (not an
edit-in-place that anchors to existing content), the resolved file:line of
the new block is sometimes data downstream tasks need to reference. Three
mechanisms were proposed initially:

1. Interprocess file (`.checklist-lineno-handoff.json`).
2. CHECKLIST.md amendment with orchestrator's blessing.
3. Direct dispatch-return: coder emits resolved positions in stdout as part
   of its standard report.

**Refinement (2026-05-06)**: Don't invent a new IPC channel. The current
coder-dispatch prompt template requires:

> Report: CHECKLIST diff, Do/Verify output, any halt.

Extend the requirement:

> Report: CHECKLIST diff, Do/Verify output, any halt. **And any line numbers /
> anchor positions downstream tasks will need to reference, on successful
> completion as well as on halt.**

Coder emits e.g. `RESOLVED: <task-id> → <file>:<line> [anchor=<name>]` as
part of its normal report. Orchestrator parses these out of stdout and
threads them into subsequent dispatch prompts. Mechanism (1) and (2) are
deprecated as over-engineered.

**Edge cases dissolved by the refinement**: race between concurrent coders
writing IPC and orchestrator reading; stale-anchor cleanup discipline
(positions are never persisted on disk); detection of an anchor's
containing block being deleted (degrades to pure orchestrator-state
concern).

**Edge cases that remain (the agenda for the architect cycle that promotes
AP-5 from DRAFT to adopted)**:

1. Anchor naming collisions across concurrent coders — manageable by
   requiring anchors to include task-id, but not yet specified as a hard
   rule.
2. What happens when a coder's commented anchor becomes a later task's
   `old_string` Edit target — anchor strings need to be picked so they're
   not Edit-target candidates; pattern-design question.
3. Orchestrator's own state management — has to absorb reported positions
   into the next-wave dispatch prompts; needs an explicit pattern, not
   ad-hoc.
4. Empirical pressure: 2026-05-06's dispatch hit several "file modified
   since read" Edit-tool races on CHECKLIST.md when many parallel coders
   flipped markers simultaneously. Whether anchor-based content matching
   would help, or whether marker-flip atomicity is a separate concern.

**Effect on INC-2**: Marked DRAFT, not adopted, but raised here so the
architect cycle that ratifies it has a concrete starting point. The
2026-05-06 swarm dispatch did not actually require AP-5 — every offending
clause was an Accept-clause shape (AP-1..AP-4), not a position-handoff
shape. AP-5 is forward-looking; AP-1..AP-4 are the load-bearing remediation
of INC-2.

---

## Tradeoff / honest counter-argument

Closing every Accept clause to AP-3's palette removes **end-to-end runtime
verification** from the swarm dispatch surface. A naive reading would say
"now the swarm only verifies that the code compiles, not that it runs" —
and that's correct, in the sense that swarm-side verification covers
*structural* correctness (compile, content, commit reachability) and not
*behavioural* correctness (does the recording actually start, does the
permission dialog actually appear).

The tradeoff is deliberate. Behavioural verification is **better** when it
runs as an Operator verification protocol than when it runs as a swarm task,
for two reasons:

1. **Scope visibility**: a CHECKLIST task that says "tap Start, observe
   recording, tap Stop" hides from the operator that they will be tapping a
   button. They see a swarm complete, assume the work is done, and discover
   on next launch that nobody actually verified the runtime path. The
   Operator verification protocol carve-out (AP-4) makes the manual step
   explicit and visible.

2. **Reliability under repetition**: an `adb logcat` filter that's
   expected to be empty 99% of the time tells the operator nothing on the
   1st run, the 10th run, or the 100th. A compile gate that fails when
   the code is wrong tells the operator something every time. The two
   verifications are complementary; collapsing them into one swarm task
   loses the complement.

The cost of SC2 is that the CHECKLIST becomes incomplete *on its own* —
it does not, alone, certify that the project runs. It certifies that the
project compiles, that its files are present and tracked, that its commit
graph is intact. Runtime certification lives elsewhere (in the DL's
Operator verification protocol sub-section, in the operator's manual
post-swarm walkthrough, in CI integration tests when those exist). This
is the right shape for a swarm-dispatchable contract; a CHECKLIST that
tries to certify runtime as well as structure cannot be swarmed.

---

## Applied (DeepScriber, 2026-05-06)

DeepScriber adopted SC2 in commit `67a671d`. The mechanical edits were:

1. **`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`** — new DL-14 codifying AP-1..AP-4 in DeepScriber-
   local language. DL-5 / DL-9 / DL-11 / DL-12 each had their procedural-
   verification clauses rewritten or deleted.
2. **`CHECKLIST.md`** — 7 deletions (L1, L2, B4, MM5b, M-LR6, M-VRY,
   T-1..T-6); 5 idempotent rewrites (B0a, B0d, B3, M-LRT4, M-LRT5);
   timestamped backup of the pre-refactor state preserved.
3. **Swarm validation** — 28 coder dispatches across 4 waves, 107 ✅, zero
   halts.
4. **Project memory** — `learning_idempotent_accept_clauses.md` +
   `feedback_no_diagnosing_in_code_mode.md` recorded in
   `~/.claude/projects/-home-robin-forgejo-DeepScriber/memory/`.

For a project adopting SC2 fresh:

1. Audit `CHECKLIST.md`: `grep -nE 'adb logcat|git status --short|tap '
   CHECKLIST.md` and similar; flag every match as a candidate for
   AP-1..AP-2 violation.
2. For each flagged task: rewrite using AP-3 palette, OR delete + replace
   with an Operator verification protocol entry in the DL where the
   architectural decision lives (AP-4).
3. Audit `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` DL entries: `grep -nE 'adb logcat|adb
   install|tap |observe in logcat' DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` — flag every match
   as a DL prescribing an anti-idempotent gate.
4. For each flagged DL: revise the prescription to drop the procedural
   verification (keep the architectural decision); add an `**Operator
   verification protocol**` sub-section if runtime walkthrough is
   genuinely required.
5. Validate by attempting a swarm dispatch of all unfinished tasks. The
   adoption is complete when zero halts occur.
6. Record adoption in the project's `CLAUDE.md` (citing `SC2`) and add an
   AD entry to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` recording the convention adoption
   itself.

---

## Versioning

- 1.0 (2026-05-06): Initial adoption. AP-1..AP-4 are load-bearing.
  AP-5 is DRAFT, awaiting architect-cycle ratification.
