1	# SC4 — Final Test Rubric / Gauntlet (GR-1..GR-7)
2	
3	- **Version**: 1.0
4	- **Date**: 2026-06-13
5	- **Status**: Adopted (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-19; complements SC2 + TC11)
6	- **Precipitating incident(s)**: pearl-wallet-android v1.74.88291 — biometric unlock **succeeded**, then a redundant manual passphrase box appeared anyway. A runtime **sequence** defect (correct screens, wrong order) that no structural CHECKLIST `Accept` clause can catch and that a screencast of the run made first-class reviewable. Shared with TC11 (`../TOOLING_CONVENTIONS/gauntlet-screencast-archival.md`); carried there by orchestrator decision (see "Incident grounding" below).
7	- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation: PLAN pre-commits criteria); I-12 (NO PROXY EVER: direct semantic evaluation)
8	- **Companion to**: SC2 (Idempotent Accept Clauses) — SC2 certifies STRUCTURE, SC4 certifies RUNTIME; SC2's tradeoff explicitly punts runtime certification "elsewhere," and SC4 IS that elsewhere; TC11 (Gauntlet Screencast Archival) — the evidence mechanic every SC4 run cites; SC2 AP-4 (Operator verification protocol) — the same agent/operator boundary, lifted from a DL sub-section to a first-class rubric row
9	- **Applies to**: every project that produces a release artifact requiring end-to-end runtime certification (mobile/desktop/web apps, signed packages, device-facing firmware). Pure-library projects may scope the rubric to integration/property tests; the timing, verdict, and attestation disciplines still bind.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Problem statement
14	
15	A swarm-dispatchable `CHECKLIST.md` (SC2) certifies that the project **compiles, that its files are present and tracked, and that its commit graph is intact** — i.e. structural correctness. SC2's tradeoff section states this plainly and concedes:
16	
17	> The CHECKLIST becomes incomplete *on its own* — it does not, alone, certify that the project runs. ... Runtime certification lives elsewhere.
18	
19	That "elsewhere" had no convention of its own. Without one, end-to-end runtime acceptance was improvised per project: success criteria were written after the fact to match whatever the code did; defects were waived into a "known-open, don't-block" third state that shipped anyway; PASS verdicts were granted on `logcat` greps that proxy over the actual UI (an I-12 violation at the moment of release, when it is most expensive). The pearl-wallet-android v1.74.88291 biometric-sequence defect — bio success followed by a redundant passphrase box — is the precipitating instance: correct screens, wrong order, invisible to every structural `Accept` clause, caught only because the operator was watching the device live and the run was screencasted.
20	
21	SC4 closes that gap. It defines the required **shape** of a project's final test rubric — `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` — so that end-to-end runtime acceptance is a PLAN-phase deliverable with a pre-committed, two-outcome, semantically-attested contract, executed once the structural contract (CHECKLIST) is fully satisfied.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## The seven properties
26	
27	Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the closed form required, (c) the structural effect on the precipitating incident.
28	
29	### GR-1 — Authored-at-PLAN (a sibling deliverable to CHECKLIST.md)
30	
31	The rubric is written during PLAN, concurrently with `CHECKLIST.md`, so success criteria are pre-committed before any CODE exists.
32	
33	**Permissive form**: rubric improvised post-hoc after CODE completes, drafted to match the behaviour the code happens to exhibit; or absent entirely, with "we'll just test it on the device when it's done."
34	
35	**Closed form required**: `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` exists as a PLAN-phase artifact, written before CODE begins. Its existence and row set are part of the architect exit gate alongside the CHECKLIST: a project entering CODE without a rubric has not exited PLAN.
36	
37	**Effect**: success criteria cannot drift to retro-fit the implementation. The biometric-sequence defect is uncatchable by a rubric that only specifies "unlock works"; a PLAN-authored rubric that specifies "biometric success completes unlock with no passphrase dialog afterwards" (as the pearl exemplar's A4 does) makes the sequence a first-class requirement before any code exists to bias the wording.
38	
39	### GR-2 — Run-after-all-✅ (execution timing)
40	
41	The gauntlet is executed only after every `CHECKLIST.md` task is ✅.
42	
43	**Permissive form**: running gauntlet items mid-CODE to "check progress," or running them before the swarm has finished wiring.
44	
45	**Closed form required**: the gauntlet run begins after the CHECKLIST is fully attested (all tasks ✅, not merely `[X]`). Partial-state gauntlet runs are not verdicts; they are debugging.
46	
47	**Effect**: the gauntlet tests the integrated product, not a half-wired intermediate. A defect found mid-CODE on incomplete wiring is a false signal; a defect found after all ✅ is a true runtime defect requiring a return to ARCHITECT/CODE. The timing rule makes the gauntlet's signal trustworthy.
48	
49	### GR-3 — Two-outcome verdict doctrine (no waiver state)
50	
51	A completed gauntlet admits exactly two terminal verdicts: **SHIP-READY** or **DEFECTIVE**.
52	
53	**Permissive form**: a third "KNOWN-OPEN, don't block release" waiver category that lets a defective item ship with a footnote.
54	
55	**Closed form required**: exactly two terminal verdicts. Any ❌ at any severity ⇒ DEFECTIVE. There is no waived state; formerly-open defects are regression items that must PASS. Severity (BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) ranks fix urgency, it does not waive the verdict.
56	
57	**Effect**: the biometric-sequence defect — formerly the kind of item waivered into a release — cannot ship. The verdict doctrine converts "known-open" from a release lever into a to-do that blocks until green.
58	
59	### GR-3a — INCOMPLETE—pending-operator (the only reportable non-terminal state)
60	
61	The agent-executable subset all-passing while the operator-gated subset remains un-run yields **INCOMPLETE—pending-operator**, never silently SHIP-READY.
62	
63	**Permissive form**: a run whose agent items all pass is reported as ready, with operator-gated items implied or omitted.
64	
65	**Closed form required**: a run is SHIP-READY only when every row — agent-executed AND operator-executed — is ✅. Operator-gated items remaining ⇒ INCOMPLETE—pending-operator, with the report enumerating exactly which IDs remain and what each needs.
66	
67	**Effect**: the agent cannot grant itself a clean bill of health on the subset it can reach; the operator-gated subset (the biometric itself, funds, camera-at-paper) is an explicit, enumerated gate, not a gap.
68	
69	### GR-4 — Semantic PASS (I-12 inheritance)
70	
71	A PASS is granted by **direct semantic observation** of the evidence — a screenshot, UI-dump, or observed behaviour judged against the requirement — never by a proxy.
72	
73	**Permissive form**: a `logcat` grep that returns the expected string ⇒ PASS; "no `FATAL EXCEPTION`" ⇒ stable; a build success ⇒ "it works."
74	
75	**Closed form required**: a PASS is granted by *looking at* the evidence and judging it. Logs/greps are **FAIL-triggers and supporting evidence only** — a `FATAL EXCEPTION` in logcat is a valid FAIL; the absence of one is never, alone, a PASS. This is I-12 (NO PROXY EVER) specialized to the gauntlet's release moment.
76	
77	**Effect**: the biometric-sequence defect produces clean logcat (bio succeeded; the passphrase box is a UI state, not an exception). A logcat-grep PASS would wave it through; a semantic PASS — looking at the screen after bio success and seeing the spurious box — catches it.
78	
79	### GR-4a — Status markers are claims, not evidence (added 2026-07-29)
80	
81	GR-4 governs *rubric rows*. The same proxy failure recurs one layer up, at the **checklist**, and must be closed there too.
82	
83	**Permissive form**: reading task completion off `CHECKLIST.md` — grepping or counting `[X]` / `✅` / `[✓]` markers — and reporting "N of M tasks verified." Also: an `Accept` clause satisfied by a grep on committed source, treated as certifying behaviour.
84	
85	**Closed form required**: **a status marker records a claim; only the artifact is evidence.** A `[X]` → `✅` transition requires reading the artifact and judging it against its `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 entity row, then stating in one's own words what it was observed to do. Counting markers establishes that a glyph was typed into a file — nothing more. An `Accept` grep (SC2 AP-3) certifies *structure* and is a legitimate structural gate; it is never, alone, a semantic PASS.
86	
87	**Both failure directions are real, and they compound**:
88	- A marker flipped over a broken or partial implementation reads as **done** — the grep entrenches the defect and the next reader inherits it as ground truth.
89	- A correct implementation whose marker carries a typo, a different glyph, or an unexpected spacing reads as **not done** — provoking rework of finished work, or worse, a second parallel implementation.
90	
91	**Effect**: the count is stable and cheap and therefore seductive, which is exactly why it displaces the reading it stands in for. Structurally, a marker is downstream of the artifact (someone read something, then typed a character); treating it as upstream inverts the evidence chain. The rule restores the direction: read the artifact, then trust the marker — never the reverse.
92	
93	*Precipitating instance (2026-07-29, Kintsugi-Unbroken BUG wave):* an orchestrator reported "46 of 49 tasks verified" from `grep -c '\*\*Status:\*\* \[✓\]'` across five checklist fragments, and planned a release build on that basis, while the tree in question carried none of the fixes. Operator: *"you are not to use greps for proxies to semantic evaluation of code because it ALWAYS ends up entrenching broken and part-implementations and calling it done — and slight misspellings as not done."*
94	
95	### GR-5 — Row schema
96	
97	Every rubric item is a table row:
98	
99	`ID | Requirement | Driver | Steps / PASS criteria | Severity`
100	
101	- **Driver** ∈ {**AUTO** (agent-executable end-to-end), **OPERATOR** (not agent-executable — see GR-6), **COND** (conditional on environment or a precondition, e.g. balance > 0, app installed)}.
102	- **Severity** ∈ {**BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW**}.
103	- **PASS criteria** are concrete and observable: the exact string, the exact UI state, the exact before/after. "Works correctly" is not a criterion.
104	
105	Any ❌ at any severity ⇒ DEFECTIVE (GR-3). ⚠️ PARTIAL on a BLOCKER/HIGH item counts as ❌.
106	
107	**Effect**: the schema forces each requirement into an executable, observable, severity-ranked form at PLAN time — the same closure SC1 applies to spec prose and SC2 applies to Accept clauses.
108	
109	### GR-6 — Operator-gated carve-out
110	
111	Items genuinely not agent-executable — hardware biometric, real-funds sends, camera-at-paper OCR, network cut that would sever the control link, destructive actions without authorization — are enumerated as `Driver = OPERATOR` rows and surfaced in the run hand-off.
112	
113	**Permissive form**: operator-gated items buried inside AUTO rows as "(operator taps here)," or omitted because "the agent can't do it."
114	
115	**Closed form required**: every non-agent-executable requirement is its own OPERATOR row, enumerated in the run report's hand-off. This is the same boundary as SC2 AP-4's "Operator verification protocol" — lifted from a DL sub-section to a first-class, severity-ranked rubric row that counts toward the verdict (an un-run OPERATOR row ⇒ INCOMPLETE—pending-operator under GR-3a).
116	
117	**Effect**: the operator's manual surface is visible and counted, not implicit. The agent cannot hide behind "that part is your job" to reach SHIP-READY.
118	
119	### GR-7 — Evidence + honour-staking attestation
120	
121	The run leaves viewable, annotatable evidence and ends with an attestation block that stakes the attester's honour.
122	
123	**Permissive form**: a run report that states verdicts in prose, with no artifacts a reviewer can replay; no attestation.
124	
125	**Closed form required**:
126	- Agent captures go to gitignored `.tmp/`; the committed run report cites **every** verdict's evidence file by name (a verdict whose evidence file does not exist is not a verdict).
127	- Secret-bearing captures (mnemonic grids, passphrases, keys) are quarantined to `.tmp/` and referenced by filename + sha256 only — never committed (HR-6 secret hygiene, inherited via TC11).
128	- The whole driven session is screencast-recorded per **TC11** — the screencast captures *sequences* (what appeared after what) that stills cannot; segments archived under `dist/rubric-runs/`.
129	- The run report ends with an **attestation block**: who/what ran it, when, against which build and device, the verdict, and the explicit statement that every ✅ was granted on direct observation of the cited evidence (GR-4).
130	
131	**Effect**: a reviewer — the operator, a future architect, an auditor — can replay the run, scrub the screencast, and judge each verdict against its evidence rather than trusting prose. The attestation makes "nothing was missed" a staked claim, not an aspiration.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Relation to SC2 and I-7
136	
137	SC2 (I-7) and SC4 certify **different things**:
138	
139	| | Certifies | Mechanism | When |
140	|---|---|---|---|
141	| **SC2 / I-7** | STRUCTURE | idempotent end-state: compile, grep, git | per-task, during CODE |
142	| **SC4 / I-19** | RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR | semantic observation of driven evidence | once, after all ✅ |
143	
144	They are complements; neither replaces the other. SC2's tradeoff explicitly punts runtime certification "elsewhere"; SC4 is that elsewhere. A project that has all-CHECKLIST-✅ but no gauntlet run has certified that it compiles, not that it works.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## Tradeoff / honest counter-argument
149	
150	The gauntlet is **expensive and late**. It runs after CODE, so it cannot catch defects cheaply or early — every defect it surfaces has already paid the full CODE cost, and a DEFECTIVE verdict returns work to ARCHITECT/CODE at the worst moment. It costs operator time (the OPERATOR subset is, definitionally, not automatable), device soak, and on funds-bearing paths, real money at risk. A project with a fast CI feedback loop could argue the gauntlet is redundant ceremony.
151	
152	The tradeoff is deliberate, for three reasons that the structural contract cannot supply:
153	
154	1. **Sequences, not states.** The biometric defect had correct screens in the wrong order. Structural verification certifies states (does the unlock screen exist, does it compile); only a driven run certifies the *order* in which states appear. Stills miss this; the screencast (TC11) is the evidence type that catches it.
155	2. **The release moment is the last, most expensive place for a proxy.** I-12 forbids proxies everywhere, but a `logcat`-grep PASS at release ships the defect into the wild. GR-4 specializes I-12 to the moment its violation is most costly.
156	3. **Pre-committed criteria defeat post-hoc rationalization.** A rubric written after the code bends to justify the code (GR-1). The cost of authoring at PLAN is a few hours; the cost of shipping a sequence defect is a recalled release.
157	
158	The honest residual: **a gauntlet is only as good as its rubric.** GR-1 forces the rubric to exist and to pre-commit, but it cannot force the rubric to be *complete*. A rubric that omits a sequence path cannot catch a defect on that path. This is why the rubric is a sibling to ARCHITECTURE.md (not a substitute for it): the rubric's coverage is bounded by the architecture's enumerated surfaces. A gap in the architecture is a gap in the gauntlet.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Applied (adopting SC4 on a project)
163	
164	1. **At PLAN**, create `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md`:
165	   - Header: package/build identity under test, device/environment, version-pin statement ("version under test is pinned at run time").
166	   - Verdict doctrine block (two outcomes; INCOMPLETE—pending-operator; severity ⇒ fix urgency, not waiver).
167	   - Driver discipline (no blind coordinates — derive every action from a fresh UI-dump/screenshot; semantic PASS; evidence under `.tmp/`; secret quarantine; preconditions for destructive items).
168	   - Sections per feature area, each a GR-5 row-schema table; non-agent-executable requirements as OPERATOR rows (GR-6).
169	   - Verdict computation rules; attestation-block template.
170	2. **Cite SC4** in project `CLAUDE.md` (with the `SC4` / `I-19` citation), and add an **AD** (Architecture Decision) entry to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` recording the rubric's existence and scope.
171	3. **After every `CHECKLIST.md` task is ✅** (GR-2), run the gauntlet:
172	   - Capture evidence to gitignored `.tmp/`; screencast the whole driven session per **TC11** into `dist/rubric-runs/`.
173	   - Grant each PASS by direct semantic observation (GR-4); quarantine secret-bearing captures (GR-7/HR-6).
174	   - Write the run report to `dist/` (e.g. `dist/RUBRIC-RUN-v<VER>-<device>.md`), citing every verdict's evidence file by name, ending with the attestation block.
175	4. **Terminal verdict gates release:** SHIP-READY ⇒ release may proceed; DEFECTIVE ⇒ the named IDs return to ARCHITECT/CODE and the gauntlet is re-run; INCOMPLETE—pending-operator ⇒ the operator executes the enumerated subset and the run is completed or re-attested.
176	
177	First adopter: pearl-wallet-android (`DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` v2.0) — the concrete gauntlet this convention generalizes from.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## Incident grounding (loud non-compliance note)

# SC4 — Final Test Rubric / Gauntlet (GR-1..GR-7)

- **Version**: 1.0
- **Date**: 2026-06-13
- **Status**: Adopted (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-19; complements SC2 + TC11)
- **Precipitating incident(s)**: pearl-wallet-android v1.74.88291 — biometric unlock **succeeded**, then a redundant manual passphrase box appeared anyway. A runtime **sequence** defect (correct screens, wrong order) that no structural CHECKLIST `Accept` clause can catch and that a screencast of the run made first-class reviewable. Shared with TC11 (`../TOOLING_CONVENTIONS/gauntlet-screencast-archival.md`); carried there by orchestrator decision (see "Incident grounding" below).
- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation: PLAN pre-commits criteria); I-12 (NO PROXY EVER: direct semantic evaluation)
- **Companion to**: SC2 (Idempotent Accept Clauses) — SC2 certifies STRUCTURE, SC4 certifies RUNTIME; SC2's tradeoff explicitly punts runtime certification "elsewhere," and SC4 IS that elsewhere; TC11 (Gauntlet Screencast Archival) — the evidence mechanic every SC4 run cites; SC2 AP-4 (Operator verification protocol) — the same agent/operator boundary, lifted from a DL sub-section to a first-class rubric row
- **Applies to**: every project that produces a release artifact requiring end-to-end runtime certification (mobile/desktop/web apps, signed packages, device-facing firmware). Pure-library projects may scope the rubric to integration/property tests; the timing, verdict, and attestation disciplines still bind.

---

## Problem statement

A swarm-dispatchable `CHECKLIST.md` (SC2) certifies that the project **compiles, that its files are present and tracked, and that its commit graph is intact** — i.e. structural correctness. SC2's tradeoff section states this plainly and concedes:

> The CHECKLIST becomes incomplete *on its own* — it does not, alone, certify that the project runs. ... Runtime certification lives elsewhere.

That "elsewhere" had no convention of its own. Without one, end-to-end runtime acceptance was improvised per project: success criteria were written after the fact to match whatever the code did; defects were waived into a "known-open, don't-block" third state that shipped anyway; PASS verdicts were granted on `logcat` greps that proxy over the actual UI (an I-12 violation at the moment of release, when it is most expensive). The pearl-wallet-android v1.74.88291 biometric-sequence defect — bio success followed by a redundant passphrase box — is the precipitating instance: correct screens, wrong order, invisible to every structural `Accept` clause, caught only because the operator was watching the device live and the run was screencasted.

SC4 closes that gap. It defines the required **shape** of a project's final test rubric — `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` — so that end-to-end runtime acceptance is a PLAN-phase deliverable with a pre-committed, two-outcome, semantically-attested contract, executed once the structural contract (CHECKLIST) is fully satisfied.

---

## The seven properties

Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the closed form required, (c) the structural effect on the precipitating incident.

### GR-1 — Authored-at-PLAN (a sibling deliverable to CHECKLIST.md)

The rubric is written during PLAN, concurrently with `CHECKLIST.md`, so success criteria are pre-committed before any CODE exists.

**Permissive form**: rubric improvised post-hoc after CODE completes, drafted to match the behaviour the code happens to exhibit; or absent entirely, with "we'll just test it on the device when it's done."

**Closed form required**: `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` exists as a PLAN-phase artifact, written before CODE begins. Its existence and row set are part of the architect exit gate alongside the CHECKLIST: a project entering CODE without a rubric has not exited PLAN.

**Effect**: success criteria cannot drift to retro-fit the implementation. The biometric-sequence defect is uncatchable by a rubric that only specifies "unlock works"; a PLAN-authored rubric that specifies "biometric success completes unlock with no passphrase dialog afterwards" (as the pearl exemplar's A4 does) makes the sequence a first-class requirement before any code exists to bias the wording.

### GR-2 — Run-after-all-✅ (execution timing)

The gauntlet is executed only after every `CHECKLIST.md` task is ✅.

**Permissive form**: running gauntlet items mid-CODE to "check progress," or running them before the swarm has finished wiring.

**Closed form required**: the gauntlet run begins after the CHECKLIST is fully attested (all tasks ✅, not merely `[X]`). Partial-state gauntlet runs are not verdicts; they are debugging.

**Effect**: the gauntlet tests the integrated product, not a half-wired intermediate. A defect found mid-CODE on incomplete wiring is a false signal; a defect found after all ✅ is a true runtime defect requiring a return to ARCHITECT/CODE. The timing rule makes the gauntlet's signal trustworthy.

### GR-3 — Two-outcome verdict doctrine (no waiver state)

A completed gauntlet admits exactly two terminal verdicts: **SHIP-READY** or **DEFECTIVE**.

**Permissive form**: a third "KNOWN-OPEN, don't block release" waiver category that lets a defective item ship with a footnote.

**Closed form required**: exactly two terminal verdicts. Any ❌ at any severity ⇒ DEFECTIVE. There is no waived state; formerly-open defects are regression items that must PASS. Severity (BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) ranks fix urgency, it does not waive the verdict.

**Effect**: the biometric-sequence defect — formerly the kind of item waivered into a release — cannot ship. The verdict doctrine converts "known-open" from a release lever into a to-do that blocks until green.

### GR-3a — INCOMPLETE—pending-operator (the only reportable non-terminal state)

The agent-executable subset all-passing while the operator-gated subset remains un-run yields **INCOMPLETE—pending-operator**, never silently SHIP-READY.

**Permissive form**: a run whose agent items all pass is reported as ready, with operator-gated items implied or omitted.

**Closed form required**: a run is SHIP-READY only when every row — agent-executed AND operator-executed — is ✅. Operator-gated items remaining ⇒ INCOMPLETE—pending-operator, with the report enumerating exactly which IDs remain and what each needs.

**Effect**: the agent cannot grant itself a clean bill of health on the subset it can reach; the operator-gated subset (the biometric itself, funds, camera-at-paper) is an explicit, enumerated gate, not a gap.

### GR-4 — Semantic PASS (I-12 inheritance)

A PASS is granted by **direct semantic observation** of the evidence — a screenshot, UI-dump, or observed behaviour judged against the requirement — never by a proxy.

**Permissive form**: a `logcat` grep that returns the expected string ⇒ PASS; "no `FATAL EXCEPTION`" ⇒ stable; a build success ⇒ "it works."

**Closed form required**: a PASS is granted by *looking at* the evidence and judging it. Logs/greps are **FAIL-triggers and supporting evidence only** — a `FATAL EXCEPTION` in logcat is a valid FAIL; the absence of one is never, alone, a PASS. This is I-12 (NO PROXY EVER) specialized to the gauntlet's release moment.

**Effect**: the biometric-sequence defect produces clean logcat (bio succeeded; the passphrase box is a UI state, not an exception). A logcat-grep PASS would wave it through; a semantic PASS — looking at the screen after bio success and seeing the spurious box — catches it.

### GR-4a — Status markers are claims, not evidence (added 2026-07-29)

GR-4 governs *rubric rows*. The same proxy failure recurs one layer up, at the **checklist**, and must be closed there too.

**Permissive form**: reading task completion off `CHECKLIST.md` — grepping or counting `[X]` / `✅` / `[✓]` markers — and reporting "N of M tasks verified." Also: an `Accept` clause satisfied by a grep on committed source, treated as certifying behaviour.

**Closed form required**: **a status marker records a claim; only the artifact is evidence.** A `[X]` → `✅` transition requires reading the artifact and judging it against its `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 entity row, then stating in one's own words what it was observed to do. Counting markers establishes that a glyph was typed into a file — nothing more. An `Accept` grep (SC2 AP-3) certifies *structure* and is a legitimate structural gate; it is never, alone, a semantic PASS.

**Both failure directions are real, and they compound**:
- A marker flipped over a broken or partial implementation reads as **done** — the grep entrenches the defect and the next reader inherits it as ground truth.
- A correct implementation whose marker carries a typo, a different glyph, or an unexpected spacing reads as **not done** — provoking rework of finished work, or worse, a second parallel implementation.

**Effect**: the count is stable and cheap and therefore seductive, which is exactly why it displaces the reading it stands in for. Structurally, a marker is downstream of the artifact (someone read something, then typed a character); treating it as upstream inverts the evidence chain. The rule restores the direction: read the artifact, then trust the marker — never the reverse.

*Precipitating instance (2026-07-29, Kintsugi-Unbroken BUG wave):* an orchestrator reported "46 of 49 tasks verified" from `grep -c '\*\*Status:\*\* \[✓\]'` across five checklist fragments, and planned a release build on that basis, while the tree in question carried none of the fixes. Operator: *"you are not to use greps for proxies to semantic evaluation of code because it ALWAYS ends up entrenching broken and part-implementations and calling it done — and slight misspellings as not done."*

### GR-5 — Row schema

Every rubric item is a table row:

`ID | Requirement | Driver | Steps / PASS criteria | Severity`

- **Driver** ∈ {**AUTO** (agent-executable end-to-end), **OPERATOR** (not agent-executable — see GR-6), **COND** (conditional on environment or a precondition, e.g. balance > 0, app installed)}.
- **Severity** ∈ {**BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW**}.
- **PASS criteria** are concrete and observable: the exact string, the exact UI state, the exact before/after. "Works correctly" is not a criterion.

Any ❌ at any severity ⇒ DEFECTIVE (GR-3). ⚠️ PARTIAL on a BLOCKER/HIGH item counts as ❌.

**Effect**: the schema forces each requirement into an executable, observable, severity-ranked form at PLAN time — the same closure SC1 applies to spec prose and SC2 applies to Accept clauses.

### GR-6 — Operator-gated carve-out

Items genuinely not agent-executable — hardware biometric, real-funds sends, camera-at-paper OCR, network cut that would sever the control link, destructive actions without authorization — are enumerated as `Driver = OPERATOR` rows and surfaced in the run hand-off.

**Permissive form**: operator-gated items buried inside AUTO rows as "(operator taps here)," or omitted because "the agent can't do it."

**Closed form required**: every non-agent-executable requirement is its own OPERATOR row, enumerated in the run report's hand-off. This is the same boundary as SC2 AP-4's "Operator verification protocol" — lifted from a DL sub-section to a first-class, severity-ranked rubric row that counts toward the verdict (an un-run OPERATOR row ⇒ INCOMPLETE—pending-operator under GR-3a).

**Effect**: the operator's manual surface is visible and counted, not implicit. The agent cannot hide behind "that part is your job" to reach SHIP-READY.

### GR-7 — Evidence + honour-staking attestation

The run leaves viewable, annotatable evidence and ends with an attestation block that stakes the attester's honour.

**Permissive form**: a run report that states verdicts in prose, with no artifacts a reviewer can replay; no attestation.

**Closed form required**:
- Agent captures go to gitignored `.tmp/`; the committed run report cites **every** verdict's evidence file by name (a verdict whose evidence file does not exist is not a verdict).
- Secret-bearing captures (mnemonic grids, passphrases, keys) are quarantined to `.tmp/` and referenced by filename + sha256 only — never committed (HR-6 secret hygiene, inherited via TC11).
- The whole driven session is screencast-recorded per **TC11** — the screencast captures *sequences* (what appeared after what) that stills cannot; segments archived under `dist/rubric-runs/`.
- The run report ends with an **attestation block**: who/what ran it, when, against which build and device, the verdict, and the explicit statement that every ✅ was granted on direct observation of the cited evidence (GR-4).

**Effect**: a reviewer — the operator, a future architect, an auditor — can replay the run, scrub the screencast, and judge each verdict against its evidence rather than trusting prose. The attestation makes "nothing was missed" a staked claim, not an aspiration.

---

## Relation to SC2 and I-7

SC2 (I-7) and SC4 certify **different things**:

| | Certifies | Mechanism | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SC2 / I-7** | STRUCTURE | idempotent end-state: compile, grep, git | per-task, during CODE |
| **SC4 / I-19** | RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR | semantic observation of driven evidence | once, after all ✅ |

They are complements; neither replaces the other. SC2's tradeoff explicitly punts runtime certification "elsewhere"; SC4 is that elsewhere. A project that has all-CHECKLIST-✅ but no gauntlet run has certified that it compiles, not that it works.

---

## Tradeoff / honest counter-argument

The gauntlet is **expensive and late**. It runs after CODE, so it cannot catch defects cheaply or early — every defect it surfaces has already paid the full CODE cost, and a DEFECTIVE verdict returns work to ARCHITECT/CODE at the worst moment. It costs operator time (the OPERATOR subset is, definitionally, not automatable), device soak, and on funds-bearing paths, real money at risk. A project with a fast CI feedback loop could argue the gauntlet is redundant ceremony.

The tradeoff is deliberate, for three reasons that the structural contract cannot supply:

1. **Sequences, not states.** The biometric defect had correct screens in the wrong order. Structural verification certifies states (does the unlock screen exist, does it compile); only a driven run certifies the *order* in which states appear. Stills miss this; the screencast (TC11) is the evidence type that catches it.
2. **The release moment is the last, most expensive place for a proxy.** I-12 forbids proxies everywhere, but a `logcat`-grep PASS at release ships the defect into the wild. GR-4 specializes I-12 to the moment its violation is most costly.
3. **Pre-committed criteria defeat post-hoc rationalization.** A rubric written after the code bends to justify the code (GR-1). The cost of authoring at PLAN is a few hours; the cost of shipping a sequence defect is a recalled release.

The honest residual: **a gauntlet is only as good as its rubric.** GR-1 forces the rubric to exist and to pre-commit, but it cannot force the rubric to be *complete*. A rubric that omits a sequence path cannot catch a defect on that path. This is why the rubric is a sibling to ARCHITECTURE.md (not a substitute for it): the rubric's coverage is bounded by the architecture's enumerated surfaces. A gap in the architecture is a gap in the gauntlet.

---

## Applied (adopting SC4 on a project)

1. **At PLAN**, create `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md`:
   - Header: package/build identity under test, device/environment, version-pin statement ("version under test is pinned at run time").
   - Verdict doctrine block (two outcomes; INCOMPLETE—pending-operator; severity ⇒ fix urgency, not waiver).
   - Driver discipline (no blind coordinates — derive every action from a fresh UI-dump/screenshot; semantic PASS; evidence under `.tmp/`; secret quarantine; preconditions for destructive items).
   - Sections per feature area, each a GR-5 row-schema table; non-agent-executable requirements as OPERATOR rows (GR-6).
   - Verdict computation rules; attestation-block template.
2. **Cite SC4** in project `CLAUDE.md` (with the `SC4` / `I-19` citation), and add an **AD** (Architecture Decision) entry to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` recording the rubric's existence and scope.
3. **After every `CHECKLIST.md` task is ✅** (GR-2), run the gauntlet:
   - Capture evidence to gitignored `.tmp/`; screencast the whole driven session per **TC11** into `dist/rubric-runs/`.
   - Grant each PASS by direct semantic observation (GR-4); quarantine secret-bearing captures (GR-7/HR-6).
   - Write the run report to `dist/` (e.g. `dist/RUBRIC-RUN-v<VER>-<device>.md`), citing every verdict's evidence file by name, ending with the attestation block.
4. **Terminal verdict gates release:** SHIP-READY ⇒ release may proceed; DEFECTIVE ⇒ the named IDs return to ARCHITECT/CODE and the gauntlet is re-run; INCOMPLETE—pending-operator ⇒ the operator executes the enumerated subset and the run is completed or re-attested.

First adopter: pearl-wallet-android (`DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` v2.0) — the concrete gauntlet this convention generalizes from.

---

## Incident grounding (loud non-compliance note)

The SPEC_CONVENTIONS "how to propose a new convention" rule states: *"Identify the precipitating incident(s) in `INCIDENTS.md`. No incident = no convention."* SC4's precipitating incident is **real and documented** (operator-witnessed, 2026-06-12) but **lives in TC11, not in a dedicated `INCIDENTS.md` entry** — by orchestrator decision (the dispatch directs "use the shared TC11 incident; do not invent incidents"). This complies with the rule's *purpose* (every convention is grounded in a real, witnessed failure) while deviating from its *wording* (the path). Recorded loudly per the purposive-rule-reading ideology rather than silently reinterpreted. **Recommendation for the orchestrator:** either (a) split the biometric-sequence incident into its own `INCIDENTS/` file and have both SC4 and TC11 cite it, or (b) amend the "how to propose" rule to permit an incident carried by a sibling convention doc. Neither blocks adoption.

---

## Versioning

- 1.0 (2026-06-13): Initial adoption. GR-1..GR-7 are load-bearing. Companion to SC2 (I-7) and TC11; backstops I-12 at the release moment; cited by spine rule I-19.

1	# SC2 — Idempotent Accept Clauses (AP-1..AP-5)
2	
3	- **Version**: 1.0
4	- **Date**: 2026-05-06
5	- **Status**: Adopted (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-7 landed 2026-05-06)
6	- **Precipitating incident(s)**: [INC-2 — The Swarm-Blocker Accept Clauses](../INCIDENTS/swarm-blocker-accept-clauses.md)
7	- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation)
8	- **Companion to**: SC1 (Closed Spec Properties); SC1 closes the *shape* a spec must take, SC2 closes the *shape* a CHECKLIST `Accept` clause must take; SC4 (Final Test Rubric / Gauntlet) closes the *shape* of the post-CODE runtime gauntlet — SC2's tradeoff punts runtime certification to SC4
9	- **Applies to**: every project that uses the four-phase MAP→ARCHITECT→PLAN→CODE workflow with a `CHECKLIST.md` contract
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Problem statement
14	
15	`CHECKLIST.md` is the contract for CODE-phase execution. Each task carries
16	`Files`/`Do`/`Verify`/`Accept` fields; coders read the contract, perform
17	`Do`, run `Verify`, observe `Accept`, and flip the marker.
18	
19	The canonical **four-stage marker discipline** is:
20	
21	> `[ ]` Task → `[/]` Undertaken Task → `[X]` Completed Task → `✅` Orchestrator-semantically-validated-as-complete Task
22	
23	`[ ]` is a one-coder-one-task-capable logical execution block formulated by an
24	architect (the sum-total of `[ ]` tasks comprises the assembly of
25	`ARCHITECTURE.md`); `[/]` is flipped by the assigned coder to acknowledge
26	Orchestrator assignment (task line suffixed with the coder session id where
27	possible); `[X]` is flipped by the coder on completion; `✅` is flipped only by
28	the Orchestrator upon semantic validation of the logical group of tasks. **The
29	logic: each of Orchestrator, Architect, Coder assigns work to a group other
30	than itself to execute, and each's work is checked by other than itself** —
31	assignment, execution, and validation are always separated across roles (I-12
32	generalized; provenance ledgered per step in the Postgres `task_ledger`).
33	
34	The discipline's original three-stage statement (`[ ]` → `[X]` → `✅`, with
35	`✅` only after `Verify` runs and matches `Accept`) was designed for sequential
36	single-coder execution. It treats the Accept clause as **a single-shot
37	observation made at the moment the task lands**.
38	
39	Single-shot observation is necessary but not sufficient for **swarm
40	dispatch**. When 14 coders run in parallel, when a coder picks up a task on a
41	fresh clone where prior coders already landed the work, when an architect
42	cycle revisits a previously-✅'d task — the Accept clause is observed many
43	times across many starting states. If the clause's truth value depends on
44	*which* starting state is observed, the swarm halts on whichever observation
45	sees the inconsistent truth.
46	
47	INC-2 (2026-05-06) traces the concrete cost: seven anti-idempotent `Accept`
48	clauses in DeepScriber's CHECKLIST.md halted a swarm dispatch in eight
49	places. The same CHECKLIST after the seven clauses were rewritten to
50	idempotent end-state assertions ran 28 coder dispatches across 4 waves with
51	**zero halts**.
52	
53	The current `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` invariants I-1..I-6 (pre-2026-05-06) do not
54	constrain the shape of an Accept clause. I-5 ("verify by running") is
55	consistent with `adb logcat` filters that depend on logcat ring-buffer state,
56	with `git status --short` reads that depend on working-tree dirtiness, with
57	manual UI taps. The gap is between "verify by running once" (the original
58	framing) and "verify by running idempotently from any starting state" (what
59	swarm dispatch requires).
60	
61	This convention closes that gap. An Accept clause that satisfies AP-1..AP-4
62	is **observably equivalent under any starting state including the
63	post-success state** — the property a swarm dispatch demands.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## The five properties
68	
69	Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the
70	closed form required, (c) the structural effect on `INC-2`.
71	
72	### AP-1 — Idempotent end-state assertion (the core property)
73	
74	Every `Accept` clause must observe **committed, durable end-state** rather
75	than transient intermediate state.
76	
77	**Permissive form** (currently allowed in DeepScriber `CHECKLIST.md` pre-DL-14):
78	
79	> **B3 Accept** (line 1791): app is visible on device, logcat shows Koin
80	> initialization with no `RuntimeException`
81	
82	**Closed form required**:
83	
84	> **B3 Accept** (post-DL-14 revision): `./gradlew :androidApp:compileDebugKotlin`
85	> reports `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`; `grep -c 'single<'
86	> androidApp/src/main/kotlin/di/AppModule.kt` reports a positive integer.
87	
88	**Effect on INC-2**: A coder picking up B3 on a fresh clone, on a clone where
89	the work already landed, or after re-running the task five times, observes
90	the same Accept result every time. The original clause was observation-of-
91	ring-buffer; the closed clause is observation-of-committed-source. The first
92	ages; the second does not.
93	
94	### AP-2 — Forbidden anti-patterns
95	
96	The following Accept-clause shapes are **forbidden** in any swarm-
97	dispatchable CHECKLIST:
98	
99	1. **Transient state observation** — `adb logcat` ring buffer reads;
100	   `git status --short` working-tree dirtiness; HTTP responses from
101	   external services that may rate-limit, deauthenticate, or restructure
102	   without notice; `top` / `ps` snapshots.
103	2. **Operator-gated checks** — manual UI taps on a phone; "open browser
104	   and check"; "install APK on a connected device and observe"; visual
105	   inspection of any kind.
106	3. **Smoke tests that double-verify** — any task whose Accept clause
107	   re-asserts a property already covered by another task's per-task
108	   gate. Example: a "shared module compiles" gate at end-of-STEP when
109	   every individual STEP task already runs `./gradlew :shared:compileTask`
110	   itself.
111	4. **Anti-idempotent commit/release Do blocks** — `git add` + `git commit`
112	   as the entire Do block. Works the first time; fails (or produces an
113	   empty commit) every subsequent time. Replace with a commit-reachability
114	   assertion (see AP-3).
115	
116	**Effect on INC-2**: Each of the seven offending clauses falls into exactly
117	one of these four buckets. The taxonomy is exhaustive over the observed
118	failure cases and predictive over the as-yet-unobserved ones (e.g., a future
119	clause that polls a Slack webhook for a deploy notification would fail under
120	AP-2.1 as soon as it's drafted).
121	
122	### AP-3 — Allowed palette (idempotent end-state forms)
123	
124	The following Accept-clause shapes are **allowed**:
125	
126	1. **Compile gate** — `./gradlew <module>:compileTask` (or equivalent)
127	   ending in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. The compile output observes committed
128	   source; same source produces same output across runs.
129	2. **File presence + hash** — `ls -la <path>` for existence,
130	   `sha256sum <file>` for content fingerprint. Both observe committed
131	   filesystem state.
132	3. **Content match against committed source** — `grep -c '<exact pattern>'
133	   <committed file>`. The grep operates on tracked source; same source
134	   produces same count.
135	4. **Commit reachability** — `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}` (exact
136	   SHA) or `git log --oneline | grep '<message prefix>'` (message form,
137	   stable across rebase). Both observe immutable git history.
138	5. **Tracked-in-git assertion** — `git ls-files <path> | wc -l`. Reads
139	   committed state, not working-tree state. This is the idempotent
140	   replacement for `git status` working-tree checks.
141	6. **Attribute assertion** — `git check-attr filter <path>` etc. Reads
142	   committed `.gitattributes`, idempotent across re-runs.
143	
144	**Effect on INC-2**: Every one of the seven anti-idempotent clauses rewrote
145	into one or two members of this palette in 1-3 lines of CHECKLIST.md edit
146	each. The palette is the constructive complement to AP-2's forbidden list.
147	
148	### AP-4 — Operator verification protocol carve-out
149	
150	When runtime device verification is **genuinely required** — FGS-microphone
151	end-to-end on a connected device, on-device LLM cold-load progress UI
152	rendering correctly, recording lifecycle producing an on-disk session
153	directory — the verification is recorded as an **Operator verification
154	protocol** inside the relevant DL in `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, **not** as a

181	### AP-5 — Coder→orchestrator success-report contract for position-sensitive output (DRAFT — not yet adopted)
182	
183	> **Status**: DRAFT, raised 2026-05-06, refined same-day. NOT YET adopted as
184	> doctrine — pending a dedicated architect cycle informed by a real
185	> position-sensitive coder dispatch where the rewrite-old-block pattern is
186	> provably insufficient.
187	
188	When a coder's `Do` block writes a **position-sensitive new block** (not an
189	edit-in-place that anchors to existing content), the resolved file:line of
190	the new block is sometimes data downstream tasks need to reference. Three
191	mechanisms were proposed initially:
192	
193	1. Interprocess file (`.checklist-lineno-handoff.json`).
194	2. CHECKLIST.md amendment with orchestrator's blessing.
195	3. Direct dispatch-return: coder emits resolved positions in stdout as part
196	   of its standard report.
197	
198	**Refinement (2026-05-06)**: Don't invent a new IPC channel. The current
199	coder-dispatch prompt template requires:
200	
201	> Report: CHECKLIST diff, Do/Verify output, any halt.
202	
203	Extend the requirement:
204	
205	> Report: CHECKLIST diff, Do/Verify output, any halt. **And any line numbers /
206	> anchor positions downstream tasks will need to reference, on successful
207	> completion as well as on halt.**
208	
209	Coder emits e.g. `RESOLVED: <task-id> → <file>:<line> [anchor=<name>]` as
210	part of its normal report. Orchestrator parses these out of stdout and
211	threads them into subsequent dispatch prompts. Mechanism (1) and (2) are
212	deprecated as over-engineered.
213	
214	**Edge cases dissolved by the refinement**: race between concurrent coders
215	writing IPC and orchestrator reading; stale-anchor cleanup discipline
216	(positions are never persisted on disk); detection of an anchor's
217	containing block being deleted (degrades to pure orchestrator-state
218	concern).
219	
220	**Edge cases that remain (the agenda for the architect cycle that promotes
221	AP-5 from DRAFT to adopted)**:
222	
223	1. Anchor naming collisions across concurrent coders — manageable by
224	   requiring anchors to include task-id, but not yet specified as a hard
225	   rule.
226	2. What happens when a coder's commented anchor becomes a later task's
227	   `old_string` Edit target — anchor strings need to be picked so they're
228	   not Edit-target candidates; pattern-design question.
229	3. Orchestrator's own state management — has to absorb reported positions
230	   into the next-wave dispatch prompts; needs an explicit pattern, not
231	   ad-hoc.
232	4. Empirical pressure: 2026-05-06's dispatch hit several "file modified
233	   since read" Edit-tool races on CHECKLIST.md when many parallel coders
234	   flipped markers simultaneously. Whether anchor-based content matching
235	   would help, or whether marker-flip atomicity is a separate concern.
236	
237	**Effect on INC-2**: Marked DRAFT, not adopted, but raised here so the
238	architect cycle that ratifies it has a concrete starting point. The
239	2026-05-06 swarm dispatch did not actually require AP-5 — every offending
240	clause was an Accept-clause shape (AP-1..AP-4), not a position-handoff
241	shape. AP-5 is forward-looking; AP-1..AP-4 are the load-bearing remediation
242	of INC-2.

245	
246	## Tradeoff / honest counter-argument
247	
248	Closing every Accept clause to AP-3's palette removes **end-to-end runtime
249	verification** from the swarm dispatch surface. A naive reading would say
250	"now the swarm only verifies that the code compiles, not that it runs" —
251	and that's correct, in the sense that swarm-side verification covers
252	*structural* correctness (compile, content, commit reachability) and not
253	*behavioural* correctness (does the recording actually start, does the
254	permission dialog actually appear).
255	
256	The tradeoff is deliberate. Behavioural verification is **better** when it
257	runs as an Operator verification protocol than when it runs as a swarm task,
258	for two reasons:
259	
260	1. **Scope visibility**: a CHECKLIST task that says "tap Start, observe
261	   recording, tap Stop" hides from the operator that they will be tapping a
262	   button. They see a swarm complete, assume the work is done, and discover
263	   on next launch that nobody actually verified the runtime path. The
264	   Operator verification protocol carve-out (AP-4) makes the manual step
265	   explicit and visible.
266	
267	2. **Reliability under repetition**: an `adb logcat` filter that's
268	   expected to be empty 99% of the time tells the operator nothing on the
269	   1st run, the 10th run, or the 100th. A compile gate that fails when
270	   the code is wrong tells the operator something every time. The two
271	   verifications are complementary; collapsing them into one swarm task
272	   loses the complement.
273	
274	The cost of SC2 is that the CHECKLIST becomes incomplete *on its own* —
275	it does not, alone, certify that the project runs. It certifies that the
276	project compiles, that its files are present and tracked, that its commit
277	graph is intact. Runtime certification lives elsewhere (in the DL's
278	Operator verification protocol sub-section, in the operator's manual
279	post-swarm walkthrough, in CI integration tests when those exist). This
280	is the right shape for a swarm-dispatchable contract; a CHECKLIST that
281	tries to certify runtime as well as structure cannot be swarmed.
282

1	# SC4 — Final Test Rubric / Gauntlet (GR-1..GR-7)
2	
3	- **Version**: 1.0
4	- **Date**: 2026-06-13
5	- **Status**: Adopted (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` I-19; complements SC2 + TC11)
6	- **Precipitating incident(s)**: pearl-wallet-android v1.74.88291 — biometric unlock **succeeded**, then a redundant manual passphrase box appeared anyway. A runtime **sequence** defect (correct screens, wrong order) that no structural CHECKLIST `Accept` clause can catch and that a screencast of the run made first-class reviewable. Shared with TC11 (`../TOOLING_CONVENTIONS/gauntlet-screencast-archival.md`); carried there by orchestrator decision (see "Incident grounding" below).
7	- **Derives from**: `IDEOLOGIES.md` — I2 (Idempotent Phase Separation: PLAN pre-commits criteria); I-12 (NO PROXY EVER: direct semantic evaluation)
8	- **Companion to**: SC2 (Idempotent Accept Clauses) — SC2 certifies STRUCTURE, SC4 certifies RUNTIME; SC2's tradeoff explicitly punts runtime certification "elsewhere," and SC4 IS that elsewhere; TC11 (Gauntlet Screencast Archival) — the evidence mechanic every SC4 run cites; SC2 AP-4 (Operator verification protocol) — the same agent/operator boundary, lifted from a DL sub-section to a first-class rubric row
9	- **Applies to**: every project that produces a release artifact requiring end-to-end runtime certification (mobile/desktop/web apps, signed packages, device-facing firmware). Pure-library projects may scope the rubric to integration/property tests; the timing, verdict, and attestation disciplines still bind.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Problem statement
14	
15	A swarm-dispatchable `CHECKLIST.md` (SC2) certifies that the project **compiles, that its files are present and tracked, and that its commit graph is intact** — i.e. structural correctness. SC2's tradeoff section states this plainly and concedes:
16	
17	> The CHECKLIST becomes incomplete *on its own* — it does not, alone, certify that the project runs. ... Runtime certification lives elsewhere.
18	
19	That "elsewhere" had no convention of its own. Without one, end-to-end runtime acceptance was improvised per project: success criteria were written after the fact to match whatever the code did; defects were waived into a "known-open, don't-block" third state that shipped anyway; PASS verdicts were granted on `logcat` greps that proxy over the actual UI (an I-12 violation at the moment of release, when it is most expensive). The pearl-wallet-android v1.74.88291 biometric-sequence defect — bio success followed by a redundant passphrase box — is the precipitating instance: correct screens, wrong order, invisible to every structural `Accept` clause, caught only because the operator was watching the device live and the run was screencasted.
20	
21	SC4 closes that gap. It defines the required **shape** of a project's final test rubric — `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` — so that end-to-end runtime acceptance is a PLAN-phase deliverable with a pre-committed, two-outcome, semantically-attested contract, executed once the structural contract (CHECKLIST) is fully satisfied.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## The seven properties
26	
27	Each property states (a) the permissive form currently allowed, (b) the closed form required, (c) the structural effect on the precipitating incident.
28	
29	### GR-1 — Authored-at-PLAN (a sibling deliverable to CHECKLIST.md)
30	
31	The rubric is written during PLAN, concurrently with `CHECKLIST.md`, so success criteria are pre-committed before any CODE exists.
32	
33	**Permissive form**: rubric improvised post-hoc after CODE completes, drafted to match the behaviour the code happens to exhibit; or absent entirely, with "we'll just test it on the device when it's done."
34	
35	**Closed form required**: `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` exists as a PLAN-phase artifact, written before CODE begins. Its existence and row set are part of the architect exit gate alongside the CHECKLIST: a project entering CODE without a rubric has not exited PLAN.
36	
37	**Effect**: success criteria cannot drift to retro-fit the implementation. The biometric-sequence defect is uncatchable by a rubric that only specifies "unlock works"; a PLAN-authored rubric that specifies "biometric success completes unlock with no passphrase dialog afterwards" (as the pearl exemplar's A4 does) makes the sequence a first-class requirement before any code exists to bias the wording.
38	
39	### GR-2 — Run-after-all-✅ (execution timing)
40	
41	The gauntlet is executed only after every `CHECKLIST.md` task is ✅.
42	
43	**Permissive form**: running gauntlet items mid-CODE to "check progress," or running them before the swarm has finished wiring.
44	
45	**Closed form required**: the gauntlet run begins after the CHECKLIST is fully attested (all tasks ✅, not merely `[X]`). Partial-state gauntlet runs are not verdicts; they are debugging.
46	
47	**Effect**: the gauntlet tests the integrated product, not a half-wired intermediate. A defect found mid-CODE on incomplete wiring is a false signal; a defect found after all ✅ is a true runtime defect requiring a return to ARCHITECT/CODE. The timing rule makes the gauntlet's signal trustworthy.
48	
49	### GR-3 — Two-outcome verdict doctrine (no waiver state)
50	
51	A completed gauntlet admits exactly two terminal verdicts: **SHIP-READY** or **DEFECTIVE**.
52	
53	**Permissive form**: a third "KNOWN-OPEN, don't block release" waiver category that lets a defective item ship with a footnote.
54	
55	**Closed form required**: exactly two terminal verdicts. Any ❌ at any severity ⇒ DEFECTIVE. There is no waived state; formerly-open defects are regression items that must PASS. Severity (BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) ranks fix urgency, it does not waive the verdict.
56	
57	**Effect**: the biometric-sequence defect — formerly the kind of item waivered into a release — cannot ship. The verdict doctrine converts "known-open" from a release lever into a to-do that blocks until green.
58	
59	### GR-3a — INCOMPLETE—pending-operator (the only reportable non-terminal state)
60	
61	The agent-executable subset all-passing while the operator-gated subset remains un-run yields **INCOMPLETE—pending-operator**, never silently SHIP-READY.
62	
63	**Permissive form**: a run whose agent items all pass is reported as ready, with operator-gated items implied or omitted.
64	
65	**Closed form required**: a run is SHIP-READY only when every row — agent-executed AND operator-executed — is ✅. Operator-gated items remaining ⇒ INCOMPLETE—pending-operator, with the report enumerating exactly which IDs remain and what each needs.
66	
67	**Effect**: the agent cannot grant itself a clean bill of health on the subset it can reach; the operator-gated subset (the biometric itself, funds, camera-at-paper) is an explicit, enumerated gate, not a gap.
68	
69	### GR-4 — Semantic PASS (I-12 inheritance)
70	
71	A PASS is granted by **direct semantic observation** of the evidence — a screenshot, UI-dump, or observed behaviour judged against the requirement — never by a proxy.
72	
73	**Permissive form**: a `logcat` grep that returns the expected string ⇒ PASS; "no `FATAL EXCEPTION`" ⇒ stable; a build success ⇒ "it works."
74	
75	**Closed form required**: a PASS is granted by *looking at* the evidence and judging it. Logs/greps are **FAIL-triggers and supporting evidence only** — a `FATAL EXCEPTION` in logcat is a valid FAIL; the absence of one is never, alone, a PASS. This is I-12 (NO PROXY EVER) specialized to the gauntlet's release moment.
76	
77	**Effect**: the biometric-sequence defect produces clean logcat (bio succeeded; the passphrase box is a UI state, not an exception). A logcat-grep PASS would wave it through; a semantic PASS — looking at the screen after bio success and seeing the spurious box — catches it.
78	
79	### GR-4a — Status markers are claims, not evidence (added 2026-07-29)
80	
81	GR-4 governs *rubric rows*. The same proxy failure recurs one layer up, at the **checklist**, and must be closed there too.
82	
83	**Permissive form**: reading task completion off `CHECKLIST.md` — grepping or counting `[X]` / `✅` / `[✓]` markers — and reporting "N of M tasks verified." Also: an `Accept` clause satisfied by a grep on committed source, treated as certifying behaviour.
84	
85	**Closed form required**: **a status marker records a claim; only the artifact is evidence.** A `[X]` → `✅` transition requires reading the artifact and judging it against its `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 entity row, then stating in one's own words what it was observed to do. Counting markers establishes that a glyph was typed into a file — nothing more. An `Accept` grep (SC2 AP-3) certifies *structure* and is a legitimate structural gate; it is never, alone, a semantic PASS.
86	
87	**Both failure directions are real, and they compound**:
88	- A marker flipped over a broken or partial implementation reads as **done** — the grep entrenches the defect and the next reader inherits it as ground truth.
89	- A correct implementation whose marker carries a typo, a different glyph, or an unexpected spacing reads as **not done** — provoking rework of finished work, or worse, a second parallel implementation.
90	
91	**Effect**: the count is stable and cheap and therefore seductive, which is exactly why it displaces the reading it stands in for. Structurally, a marker is downstream of the artifact (someone read something, then typed a character); treating it as upstream inverts the evidence chain. The rule restores the direction: read the artifact, then trust the marker — never the reverse.
92	
93	*Precipitating instance (2026-07-29, Kintsugi-Unbroken BUG wave):* an orchestrator reported "46 of 49 tasks verified" from `grep -c '\*\*Status:\*\* \[✓\]'` across five checklist fragments, and planned a release build on that basis, while the tree in question carried none of the fixes. Operator: *"you are not to use greps for proxies to semantic evaluation of code because it ALWAYS ends up entrenching broken and part-implementations and calling it done — and slight misspellings as not done."*
94	
95	### GR-5 — Row schema
96	
97	Every rubric item is a table row:
98	
99	`ID | Requirement | Driver | Steps / PASS criteria | Severity`
100	
101	- **Driver** ∈ {**AUTO** (agent-executable end-to-end), **OPERATOR** (not agent-executable — see GR-6), **COND** (conditional on environment or a precondition, e.g. balance > 0, app installed)}.
102	- **Severity** ∈ {**BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW**}.
103	- **PASS criteria** are concrete and observable: the exact string, the exact UI state, the exact before/after. "Works correctly" is not a criterion.
104	
105	Any ❌ at any severity ⇒ DEFECTIVE (GR-3). ⚠️ PARTIAL on a BLOCKER/HIGH item counts as ❌.
106	
107	**Effect**: the schema forces each requirement into an executable, observable, severity-ranked form at PLAN time — the same closure SC1 applies to spec prose and SC2 applies to Accept clauses.
108	
109	### GR-6 — Operator-gated carve-out
110	
111	Items genuinely not agent-executable — hardware biometric, real-funds sends, camera-at-paper OCR, network cut that would sever the control link, destructive actions without authorization — are enumerated as `Driver = OPERATOR` rows and surfaced in the run hand-off.
112	
113	**Permissive form**: operator-gated items buried inside AUTO rows as "(operator taps here)," or omitted because "the agent can't do it."
114	
115	**Closed form required**: every non-agent-executable requirement is its own OPERATOR row, enumerated in the run report's hand-off. This is the same boundary as SC2 AP-4's "Operator verification protocol" — lifted from a DL sub-section to a first-class, severity-ranked rubric row that counts toward the verdict (an un-run OPERATOR row ⇒ INCOMPLETE—pending-operator under GR-3a).
116	
117	**Effect**: the operator's manual surface is visible and counted, not implicit. The agent cannot hide behind "that part is your job" to reach SHIP-READY.
118	
119	### GR-7 — Evidence + honour-staking attestation
120	
121	The run leaves viewable, annotatable evidence and ends with an attestation block that stakes the attester's honour.
122	
123	**Permissive form**: a run report that states verdicts in prose, with no artifacts a reviewer can replay; no attestation.
124	
125	**Closed form required**:
126	- Agent captures go to gitignored `.tmp/`; the committed run report cites **every** verdict's evidence file by name (a verdict whose evidence file does not exist is not a verdict).
127	- Secret-bearing captures (mnemonic grids, passphrases, keys) are quarantined to `.tmp/` and referenced by filename + sha256 only — never committed (HR-6 secret hygiene, inherited via TC11).
128	- The whole driven session is screencast-recorded per **TC11** — the screencast captures *sequences* (what appeared after what) that stills cannot; segments archived under `dist/rubric-runs/`.
129	- The run report ends with an **attestation block**: who/what ran it, when, against which build and device, the verdict, and the explicit statement that every ✅ was granted on direct observation of the cited evidence (GR-4).
130	
131	**Effect**: a reviewer — the operator, a future architect, an auditor — can replay the run, scrub the screencast, and judge each verdict against its evidence rather than trusting prose. The attestation makes "nothing was missed" a staked claim, not an aspiration.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Relation to SC2 and I-7
136	
137	SC2 (I-7) and SC4 certify **different things**:
138	
139	| | Certifies | Mechanism | When |
140	|---|---|---|---|
141	| **SC2 / I-7** | STRUCTURE | idempotent end-state: compile, grep, git | per-task, during CODE |
142	| **SC4 / I-19** | RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR | semantic observation of driven evidence | once, after all ✅ |
143	
144	They are complements; neither replaces the other. SC2's tradeoff explicitly punts runtime certification "elsewhere"; SC4 is that elsewhere. A project that has all-CHECKLIST-✅ but no gauntlet run has certified that it compiles, not that it works.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## Tradeoff / honest counter-argument
149	
150	The gauntlet is **expensive and late**. It runs after CODE, so it cannot catch defects cheaply or early — every defect it surfaces has already paid the full CODE cost, and a DEFECTIVE verdict returns work to ARCHITECT/CODE at the worst moment. It costs operator time (the OPERATOR subset is, definitionally, not automatable), device soak, and on funds-bearing paths, real money at risk. A project with a fast CI feedback loop could argue the gauntlet is redundant ceremony.
151	
152	The tradeoff is deliberate, for three reasons that the structural contract cannot supply:
153	
154	1. **Sequences, not states.** The biometric defect had correct screens in the wrong order. Structural verification certifies states (does the unlock screen exist, does it compile); only a driven run certifies the *order* in which states appear. Stills miss this; the screencast (TC11) is the evidence type that catches it.
155	2. **The release moment is the last, most expensive place for a proxy.** I-12 forbids proxies everywhere, but a `logcat`-grep PASS at release ships the defect into the wild. GR-4 specializes I-12 to the moment its violation is most costly.
156	3. **Pre-committed criteria defeat post-hoc rationalization.** A rubric written after the code bends to justify the code (GR-1). The cost of authoring at PLAN is a few hours; the cost of shipping a sequence defect is a recalled release.
157	
158	The honest residual: **a gauntlet is only as good as its rubric.** GR-1 forces the rubric to exist and to pre-commit, but it cannot force the rubric to be *complete*. A rubric that omits a sequence path cannot catch a defect on that path. This is why the rubric is a sibling to ARCHITECTURE.md (not a substitute for it): the rubric's coverage is bounded by the architecture's enumerated surfaces. A gap in the architecture is a gap in the gauntlet.
159	
160	---

162	## Applied (adopting SC4 on a project)
163	
164	1. **At PLAN**, create `DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md`:
165	   - Header: package/build identity under test, device/environment, version-pin statement ("version under test is pinned at run time").
166	   - Verdict doctrine block (two outcomes; INCOMPLETE—pending-operator; severity ⇒ fix urgency, not waiver).
167	   - Driver discipline (no blind coordinates — derive every action from a fresh UI-dump/screenshot; semantic PASS; evidence under `.tmp/`; secret quarantine; preconditions for destructive items).
168	   - Sections per feature area, each a GR-5 row-schema table; non-agent-executable requirements as OPERATOR rows (GR-6).
169	   - Verdict computation rules; attestation-block template.
170	2. **Cite SC4** in project `CLAUDE.md` (with the `SC4` / `I-19` citation), and add an **AD** (Architecture Decision) entry to `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` recording the rubric's existence and scope.
171	3. **After every `CHECKLIST.md` task is ✅** (GR-2), run the gauntlet:
172	   - Capture evidence to gitignored `.tmp/`; screencast the whole driven session per **TC11** into `dist/rubric-runs/`.
173	   - Grant each PASS by direct semantic observation (GR-4); quarantine secret-bearing captures (GR-7/HR-6).
174	   - Write the run report to `dist/` (e.g. `dist/RUBRIC-RUN-v<VER>-<device>.md`), citing every verdict's evidence file by name, ending with the attestation block.
175	4. **Terminal verdict gates release:** SHIP-READY ⇒ release may proceed; DEFECTIVE ⇒ the named IDs return to ARCHITECT/CODE and the gauntlet is re-run; INCOMPLETE—pending-operator ⇒ the operator executes the enumerated subset and the run is completed or re-attested.
176	
177	First adopter: pearl-wallet-android (`DOCS/TEST_RUBRIC.md` v2.0) — the concrete gauntlet this convention generalizes from.

181	## Incident grounding (loud non-compliance note)
182	
183	The SPEC_CONVENTIONS "how to propose a new convention" rule states: *"Identify the precipitating incident(s) in `INCIDENTS.md`. ## 3. R11 "INSET-CALLOUTS" — viewport-overlay hover callout system

## 4. Click-on-inset-card vs click-on-chart-object; canned explanation system

- Natally character: `AtelierCharacter` inside `AtelierScene.tsx:71` (room pane = inset when chart

1. Example chart phase for signed-out landing (fixed invented intake → real engine, labeled, replaced

# Plan — R12 architecture: landing hero atelier/inset replica + branched chart education

## Context

The landing page (`marketing.html`, live entry for anonymous visitors) is missing the entire inset
natal-chart card from its sticky hero. The hero should be a working replica of the logged-in app
atelier: a **main view + smaller inset card** that swap focus between the atelier room view and the
natal chart view — identical in operation to the app, differing only in that the landing chart uses
a **clearly labeled anonymous example chart** (real chart engine, invented birth details — LC-02)
until the visitor's own onboarding chart is available.

**Root cause (verified)**: `src/marketing.tsx` hard-gates the chart pane, inset handle and placement
selector on `ownedChart` (lines 95, 101, 512, 514, 520, 536) — a sample/guest chart never existed in
any committed revision. Signed-out visitors (the entire landing audience) get room-only + a sign-in
caption. This is a requirement change (older MFRAME contracts said "no example chart"; current
LC-02 and today's operator instruction require it).

**Also reported**: the chart focus highlight dims the toroid structure (comment at
`src/components/Astrolabe3D.tsx:1313`: "Dim every non-subject material, **including the metal
frame**"). Operator correction: the **plum-and-metal frame must remain vivid and visually
impressive; only the other elements are dimmed**.

Baseline: master @ `e7732b6a`, clean tree, version.json `1.32.90532` (v1.32 badge confirmed
bottom-right on both operator screenshots — latest commit, as instructed).

## Operator process ruling (binding, from AskUserQuestion answers)

Strict staged pipeline, **no phase mixing**:
1. This turn: write the amended snapshot of the new complete codebase target as **R12 in
   `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`** (complete, stub-free, with a tabulated entity enumeration — no entity/
   variable/function may be used by coders unless tabulated there). Commit + push. **HOLD for
   operator presentation and signoff.**
2. After signoff (later instruction): produce the fully parallelizable 4-state subagent coder
   tasklist in `CHECKLIST.md` → **hold for operator signoff again**.
3. Then: parallel coder subagents → semantic evaluation of each returned generation against its
   specific 4-state task → send back to the same coder if insufficient.

## Operator design rulings (binding)

- **Explanation pipeline**: the two-path inset click is identical in operation everywhere, but the
  content pipeline branches:
  - *index.html / marketing (always) and logged-in unpaid or credit-depleted users*: swap-zoom,
    then the **prefab canned educational explanation** — the meaning of the element, **how different
    astrology regimes regard it**, and **how its meaning evolved over the ages**. No inference.
  - *Logged-in with sufficient credits*: does the same, **but also extends** to a personalized
    inferenced reading of the selected component(s) in context of the **current sky's ephemeris and
    the user's natal ephemeris**, generated by the **hosted API** and rendered dynamically by
    **Supertonic TTS**, with normal inference accounting.
- **Zoom**: the swap-zoom (existing 240ms inset→main pane scale animation) is the zoomed animated
  toggle. No camera fly-to.
- **Highlight**: dim only the other representational elements; the plum-and-metal toroid frame stays
  vivid at full opacity.

## R12 architecture content (to be written after approval)

New section `## R12 — Landing atelier/inset replica and branched chart education` in
`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, following the R11 amendment pattern, with four **independent, parallelizable
assignments** (disjoint file ownership) and a complete entity table. Outline:

### R12-A MARKETING-REPLICA — `src/marketing.tsx`, `src/marketing.css`
- New frozen entity `EXAMPLE_CHART_INPUT: NatalChartInput` (invented example birth details — e.g.
  name "Aurelia (example)", 1997-11-08 19:05, Toronto 43.6532/-79.3832, tz −5, houseSystem 'W') and
  `loadExampleChart()` using the existing local `calculateNatalChart` (vendored Swiss Ephemeris
  WASM, no network/auth). Frozen values in the entity table; coders do not invent.
- `displayedChart = ownedChart ?? exampleChart` replaces every `ownedChart` hard gate (pane
  `hidden`, `Astrolabe3D` mount, inset handle, placement select, `view` derivation at :101) so the
  inset pair, drag/persist/shelf-avoidance and scroll-aware swap (`automaticView` :96) operate for
  guests. Owned chart replaces the example through the existing Phase machinery; auth/intake change
  clears lesson/selection (existing generation guards).
- Clear labeling (LP08): the caption identifies the example as an anonymous example, never as the
  visitor's chart; restore a create-your-chart entry for signed-out visitors.
- Guest education: widen `explain()` (:441-458) / `speak()` gates so authored lessons + Supertonic
  voice work without a signed-in owner — `AuthoredEducationSession` keyed to the existing
  `GUEST_ROOM` namespace; explicit-gesture voice unlock (`voiceAllowedRef` :85) preserved; **no
  inference call ever fires on the landing**.
- Marketing-side lesson choreography: lesson start drives `view` → 'chart' (Natally's room with her
  animated character becomes the inset card), auto-revert to atelier on completion/stop/failure;
  the user's manual choice overrides and cancels auto-revert (existing `manualView` semantics).

### R12-B RENDERER-TWOPATH — `src/components/Astrolabe3D.tsx` (+ `src/services/chartFocusVisuals.ts` only if a constant must move)
- **Two-path inset click** in `onClick` (:531-584): while the chart is inset, raycast *before* the
  `activateRef` short-circuit (:549). Object hit → `onActivate()` first (swap-zoom), then
  `onToggleComponent(componentId, isMulti)` deferred until the pane transition ends (existing
  transitionend/`layoutKey` redraw; immediate under reduced motion). Empty-space hit → `onActivate()`
  only (today's behavior). Foreground behavior unchanged.
- **Toroid-clear focus dimming**: tag the static structural meshes at creation (:252-320 — torus
  bezels, floor disc, guide rings) with a frozen `userData` structure flag and exempt them in the
  dim traverse (:1313-1328) and hover variant (:1330-1353) so the plum-and-metal frame stays vivid;
  only representational elements (planet beads/glyphs, sign baubles/ticks, house spokes/badges/
  sector fills, aspect lines/tubes, NOW bodies) dim. Correct the misleading comment at :1313.

### R12-C APP-EDUCATION — `src/App.tsx`, `src/components/NatallyChatbot.tsx` (+ `src/components/ReadingStage.tsx` only if the view seam requires)
- App-side two-path choreography: an inset object click's `educationalRequest` (existing
  `handleToggleComponent` :459-470 → `setEducationalRequest` :469) swaps `presentation.view` to
  'chart' (respecting existing follow/manual-override semantics) and auto-reverts to 'atelier' on
  lesson completion/stop/failure/dismiss. Natally remains visible/animated in the room inset (no new
  sprite machinery — the room pane with `AtelierCharacter` is the inset while chart is focused).
- **Branched pipeline**: prefab authored lesson always; then, if `readPaidConversationAccess`
  (`src/services/billingAccess.ts`, consumed at `NatallyChatbot.tsx:842`) grants, extend with a
  personalized inferenced interpretation of the selected component(s) via the existing hosted
  inference services (`src/services/hostedInference.ts`, `inferenceTurn.ts`) against the user's
  natal + current-sky ephemeris, rendered as a chat message + Supertonic streaming speech with
  normal inference accounting (R3); unpaid/depleted → prefab only. Rapid-reselection cancellation,
  busy/owner/stale guards preserved.

### R12-D PREFAB-CONTENT — `src/services/authoredChartExplanations.ts`
- Extend `LessonCore` (:21) with required `regimes` and `evolution` fields and complete **every**
  entry (BODIES 14, SIGN_CORES 12, HOUSE_CORES 12, ASPECT_CORES 5) with real authored content: the
  element's meaning, how different astrological regimes/traditions regard it, and how its meaning
  evolved over the ages. Factual register preserved; **Gen Z lingo restoration stays the separate
  PREFAB-GENZ task**. No placeholder content (project rule).

### Entity table + preservation + attestation
- Tabulated enumeration of **every** existing and new entity with exact name, `file:line`, role,
  signature (verified this session: e.g. `marketing.tsx:94-101` gates, `Astrolabe3D.tsx:549`
  short-circuit, `:1313-1328` dim traverse, `authoredChartExplanations.ts:21` LessonCore,
  `chartFocusVisuals.ts:2` CHART_FOCUS, `ephemeris.ts:223` calculateNatalChart, `NatallyChatbot.tsx:1038-1075`
  educational pipeline, `presentation.ts` view rules). New entities get frozen names/signatures.
- Preservation: R11 outside-inset callouts unchanged; drag/zoom/rotation/selection/inert-pane
  accessibility; reduced motion; no autostart audio; no LLM on landing; inference only through
  existing paid access and accounting; no new providers/config; purchase/billing flows untouched;
  souvenir ReadingStage inherits renderer changes without regression.
- R12 attestation paragraph (certifies the target specification, not implementation) + the staged
  operator signoff process recorded as the delivery gate.

## Execution steps after plan approval (this round only)

1. `cp DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md.bak.<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>` (house rule — backup beside
   original, edit original in place).
2. Pin remaining `file:line` details for the inference entities (`hostedInference.ts`,
   `inferenceTurn.ts`, `billingAccess.ts`) via CodeGraph/grep while writing.
3. Write the R12 section into `DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` (stub-free, closed sets, entity table complete).
4. Record the attempt in the Postgres task_ledger per
   `DOCS/TOOLING_CONVENTIONS/task-ledger-postgres.md`.
5. Commit + push to origin (verify remote readback — standing instruction). No coding, no
   CHECKLIST.md changes.
6. **HOLD**: present R12 summary to the operator for signoff. CHECKLIST production and coder
   dispatch happen only in later instructions, each behind its own signoff gate.

## Verification

- `grep -c "TBD\|future work\|open issue" DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md` → 0 (stub-free gate).
- Every entity named in R12's prose appears in R12's table; every table `file:line` resolves
  (spot-read during writing; the architecture attestation states this was checked).
- `git status` clean after commit; `git log origin/master` shows the pushed commit hash.
- Operator signoff is the round's terminal gate — recorded, not presumed.
